The founders discuss reaching 300,000 users by year three and positioning for potential acquisition by Visa or Mastercard, claiming they have first-mover advantage in the QR code payments space with lower fees than traditional cards.

topics.text: SurfCash launched on this day with 399+ co-owners of the bank acquired during fundraising.
13,000+ people signed up for the waitlist after the founder shared a link in underground payment groups where people swap crypto for fiat.
Philippines expansion announced as live market, targeting $40 billion annual remittances with goal of capturing 1% for $300 million volume.
User acquisition targets: 50,000 users by end of 2026, 150,000 by year two, 300,000 by year three.
15% APY staking available through partnership with Pendle offering USDC staking with delta-neutral strategies.
Target market consists of three groups: local crypto earners, tourists (20% use crypto), and digital nomads, totaling 75+ million people growing 200-300% year-over-year.
QR code payments require no physical cards, eliminating forex fees, machine fees, and card fees that typically go to traditional corporations.
Token holders own the company through Marshall Islands entity where smart contract serves as literal owner and director with governance rights.
Circle partnership provides USDC grants program support, product and tech support, gasless transactions via account abstraction, and upcoming co-marketing announcement expected this week.

8G6Dy2n0CiU.tldr: Patrick Sang, a family office investor based in Hong Kong with interests in AI, robotics, and crypto, discusses Empulser (contactless power transfer technology), the Solana ecosystem, and ICM tokens on Soar. The most striking point: he believes the next 3-4 years are critical due to AI and quantum computing, moved his base to New York because Trump is pro-crypto and pro-business, and sees institutional capital entering ICM projects only after retail traders and hobbyists establish credibility.

topics.text: Patrick Sang's entry into crypto in 2015 in Toronto, meeting Vitalik Buterin and other founders when Ethereum was $98.
Family office invests across AI, robotics, biotech, and special situations, with bulk of assets in real estate; moved crypto allocation to highest level in 2025.
AI is overvalued at current $200-500 billion valuations; prefers AI-enabled software solving real problems over pure AI plays like Anthropic.
Robotics manufacturing concentrated in China due to labor costs and mentality; US cannot match $10-15k monthly wages Chinese PhDs accept for factory work.
Empulser uses contactless power transfer (CBT) technology from Swiss professors; Patrick sees it as a mega opportunity and reason for being at Breakpoint.
Three investor groups buying ICM tokens: passionate technologists, hobbyist traders, then retail; institutions arrive after 1-3 months once credibility established.
Meteora's super app ambition and partnership with Soar; needs professional management as it scales beyond early developer stage.
Defiance Finance second Soar launch has strong distribution (80 million reach) but unclear revenue model and monetization; needs clearer business fundamentals.
MCG's path forward: build MCG as a brand independent of hosts, acquire distribution partners like Defiance, create IP that survives personnel changes.

f6bDXse0hsM.tldr: B0nes, a Solana trader, discusses his evolution from hodling in 2017 to profiting through a "banking strategy" where he takes small consistent wins rather than chasing massive moonshots. His biggest insight: disciplined profit-taking and running your own race—not copying wallets or following hype—transformed him from losing money on coins like the unnamed AI token to steadily accumulating SOL despite a currently brutal market.

topics.text: Bones started crypto in 2017 buying XRP and Ethereum cheaply but didn't hold; real engagement began in 2021 after catching GameStop at $12-13, then pivoted to Solana in Q4 2024 after realizing ETH had no volume while AI coins on Solana were doing $10-25M daily.

Early Solana wins: Colin (Swarm agent) went from 150-200k to 30-40M, and Spur AI went from 200k to 20M, but Bones didn't ride full bags because seeing large numbers made him sell, which he's now learned to accept.

After losing heavily on an unnamed AI coin in December, Bones deleted all wallet-tracking lists and stopped copy-trading, realizing he had no personal conviction and was just chasing others' positions before they dumped on him.

The banking strategy: aim for $200 solid profit per day (=$64k/year); sell every green candle slightly to scrape profit and always keep dry powder; banked 250 SOL in 6 weeks at ~$200 average, growing his X following from 10k to 2k by documenting the challenge.

France taught him to clip 0.1 SOL off the top on every pump of a low-cap coin instead of sizing in heavy; this kept him from getting stuck and gave him constant capital to redeploy without emotional attachment.

Win-rate is 57-58% because he takes profit when money is on the table; $1,000 gain is real money and should be taken, not chased for bigger moves; many followers started their own banking challenge and banked 6-10k SOL.

Bitcoin is below the 314 EMA (pi-based exponential moving average) on the daily, which historically signals weakness; Bones expects a head-and-shoulders pattern to play out, with a test around 100k then a dump, with recovery not until February 2026.

Currently holding DMM and WanDev QET long-term while taking a break from active trading; farming strategies are being tested for 2026; will return to trading if Bitcoin breaks above and holds the 314 EMA with good closes.

Uses Axiom for live P&L display next to positions to trigger profit-taking; Padre is preferred for alerts, limit orders, market lighthouse (volume/token creation data), and Telegram notifications on buy zones hit.

Mike 9862 trades fibs on retraces and order blocks on high-volume coins, consistently making ~$500/day; technical analysis is more reliable now because more traders use it, setting limit and sell orders based on patterns like falling wedges.

IpJPN58swmw.tldr: The MCG podcast hosts announce their coverage plans for Met Dhabi (December 10th) and Breakpoint in Abu Dhabi, where they'll interview founders, host three panels with six projects, and provide live conference coverage. Since launching in August with zero followers, MCG has grown to 5 million impressions and 200 founder interviews, largely through early coverage of projects like Avachi, Umbra, and Loyal.

topics.text: MCG grew from zero views and followers in August to 5 million impressions, 200 founder token interviews, 6,600 fans, and an MCG China channel.
MCG's sponsors include Meteora, Viva, Moby, CLED, Dupe, Orgo, Soore, and ICM Run.

Ownership tokens and ICM are positioned as the most exciting part of crypto, with companies using onchain fundraising to bootstrap community and share business upside previously impossible with traditional venture funding.
MCG is upgrading to 1080p streaming, improving audio and video, and hiring video editors and live stream editors.
Chill will host Trader Radio Monday to Friday covering markets, charting setups, and trade setups while the hosts are at conferences.
The host and Dom will be live at Met Dhabi on December 10th and at Breakpoint, meeting teams from Soore, Metadow, Maya from Street, and Avi Patel.
The hosts will host three panels covering six different projects and potentially bring viewers on stage.

hE6LJHqZ56w.tldr: Karma Wallet is a decentralized neo-bank that lets users pay bills and rent directly from crypto wallets without conversion. Founder Amish demos live bill payment functionality, announces 1,127 users with low-six-figure volumes, and plans Europe rollout with Visa cards launching by month-end.

topics.text: Bill pay feature now live: users can pay invoices, rent, and bills directly from Solana, Ethereum, or Polygon wallets to any IBAN or USD account
Fee structure: 0.5% swap fee without Karma token, 0% swap fee if holding Karma; 0.5% bill payment fee on top; goal to eventually make it 0.1%
Current user base is 1,127 users, mostly web3-native and Karma token holders; volume in low six figures with growth accelerating
Visa cards in review with partner Rain, launching by end of month; custom fund flows will allow spending collateralized positions from DeFi
Business portal and API rolling out within weeks; closed SDK currently available for early testing with interested projects
Europe-first rollout strategy focused on localized problems like Netherlands exchange restrictions; global access available with country-specific provider limitations
Marketing strategy relies on low fees and product coverage rather than paid ads due to financial compliance delays; planning social campaigns to pay user bills

9B_MXvX0CuA.tldr: FunnMedia, maker of the Water Minder hydration app with 300K users, is rebranding its reward token from Water Miner to $FUN and migrating from the collapsed Believe ecosystem to Pump Fun on December 9th, planning to integrate the token across 10+ of their health and fitness apps while generating nearly $1M in annual revenue.

topics.text: Water Minder token earned over 1 million tokens distributed to users while burning 92,000 tokens, with 14,000 active users collecting points out of 300,000 with access.
Migration process uses migrate.fun platform, starting December 9th for two weeks, requiring 50-75% of tokens migrated to maintain liquidity, launching new contract on December 22nd on pump.fun.
Unmigrated tokens after the initial two-week period face a 20% penalty converting at 1-to-0.8 ratio, with remaining supply to be decided between treasury, lock, or burn.
23+ believe ecosystem projects migrating to Pump Fun simultaneously, including Rainmaker, Wreck, PNP, Paragon Network, Cities, and Pyro.
$FUN token rebranding from Water Miner token to serve as global reward coin across applicable apps like Fitness View, where users earn for hitting walk goals and workouts.
FunnMedia has 18 total apps with 10-11 apps applicable for $FUN integration, including Calorie (launched seven years ago, Apple 2023 award winner) and Fitness View dashboard.
Combined annual revenue across all apps is shy of breaking $1 million per year, with Water Minder being the biggest earner followed by Calorie.
FunnMedia maintains separate single-problem-solver apps rather than merging into one master app, as users search the app store for specific solutions and feature bloat reduces focus.

BfFpFONmbEI.tldr: Cypher HQ is a non-custodial neo-bank wallet with 40,000 monthly active users, built by Cube, a Coinbase veteran who previously led risk engineering there. The most striking aspect: Cypher positions itself not as a crypto card but as a global financial infrastructure play enabled by stable coins and blockchain, with plans to enable AI agent commerce and lending against DeFi collateral—features impossible in traditional banking.

topics.text: Founder's background: four years at Cypher, prior roles at Y Combinator startup Zenitz, Amazon building credit card business, and Coinbase leading risk engineering on the Coinbase Card.
Cypher launched on Base because user activity ramped up significantly in the last 18 months, not due to founder's Coinbase history.

Blockchain enables global financial infrastructure on day one, removing the geographic boundaries that plague traditional fintech; founder projects $50–100 trillion opportunity vs. $80 billion for Revolut.

Crypto cards became commoditized only recently: Visa and Mastercard would not meet with crypto companies in 2017–2020, but now cards can launch in weeks, which is dangerous because most new entrants lack proper security or banking infrastructure.

Cypher's core advantage: non-custodial wallet structure provides regulatory arbitrage; Cypher holds zero customer funds while banks settle only when money moves through Visa, unlike custodial competitors.
Cypher integrated with Moonwell lending protocol on Base: users with collateral in Moonwell can auto-borrow and spend without origination fees, enabling true composability across smart contracts.
Business metrics: 40,000 monthly active users globally, $5 million TVL moving onchain, grow at roughly 30% month-over-month, planning public verification of all metrics by late January.
Revenue sources: interchange (low-quality, temporary), forex (sustainable, currently predatory through traditional banking but Cypher building onchain forex between local stablecoins like USDC-CADC).

Token model: merchants vote every two weeks on cashback distribution; brands can bribe ve-Cipher holders for increased cashback, or buy and lock tokens long-term as adoption scales—creating buy pressure when 1,000+ brands participate.

Team: seven engineers total, all since 2022, no meetings, ship by talking to users; team owns 10% with four-year lockup from token genesis (first unlock October 5, 2026), treasury 25%, 40% via 20-year emission.
Cypher raised zero dollars from public or investors; profitable after four years, no ICO or token sale—40% of FDV allocated through 20-year emission.

Q1 2025 roadmap: chat interface for blockchain wallet interactions replacing manual clicking, AI agent e-commerce experiences, enabling payments for agents ordering on behalf of users through one-time-use smart contract cards.

Hay-c-xxulQ.tldr: Foundation Labs, founded by brothers Jonathan and David, is building AI alignment technology grounded in Christian moral principles to solve the problem of AI misalignment and deception. The founders claim their system achieves 0% attack success rate on standard AI safety benchmarks where major models like GPT-4 and Claude fail at 51-96%, using a system prompt they call "the seed" based on Biblical verses rather than traditional RLHF training.

topics.text: Jonathan's conversion experience four months prior led to the idea of grounding AI with Biblical morals to solve AI alignment problems where models prioritize self-preservation over humanity.
Anthropic's June study showed blackmail rates across models: Opus 96%, Gemini Pro 95%, Deep Seek 79%; Foundation Labs applied their alignment layer and achieved 0% attack success rate.

The alignment layer is a system prompt called "the seed" (14,000 tokens), a remix of the Lord's Prayer used in preprocessing that reduces GPT-4's baseline from 51% to 0% attack success on ARM benchmarks.
David has an undergraduate degree in programming and has been in crypto since 2017; Jonathan has no AI background; they are currently building alone as a two-person team.
The product has a memory system where users can add conversations to persistent AI memory that persists across 577+ sessions and allows editing of core reasoning parameters.

WvSORe9IPjI.tldr: Viva, a telecom-backed token on Solana integrated into Bolivia's 3.1M-user Alva app, offers 20% APY staking rewards funded by real ad revenue buybacks ($110K in open market purchases so far). The project is in phase three ecosystem activation with over 11,000 holders, mostly Bolivians, and functions as both a savings incentive and utility token for accessing services like AI subscriptions that can't be purchased with local currency.

topics.text: 11,000+ Viva holders with majority being Bolivians: real employees, their families, and friends, representing early adoption in a country with millions of people.

Viva roadmap phases: phase one launched on Solana, phase two integrated wallet, phase three is full ecosystem activation with real-world integration and ad revenue buybacks, phase four expands to Mexico, US, and other countries.
Viva stakers earn 20% APY with staking rewards purchased on open market from real user demand and funded by company buybacks.
November buybacks: $40,000 from staking program plus $70,000 from Bolivian employee purchases equals $110,000 total open market buying pressure.
Alva app generates $350 million in ad revenue with average user time on app at 2.5 hours, nearly $1 million daily ad revenue.
Viva enables access to AI subscriptions like ChatGPT which cannot be purchased with Bolivianos in Bolivia, creating real spending demand beyond speculation.
Wallet onboarding is being throttled with controlled spikes to test infrastructure and ensure system stability before scaling.
Only 2.5 million Viva in circulation at $100M market cap versus Avichi at $100M with more supply, suggesting significant repricing potential if daily volume increases.

f8TE57N5FM0.tldr: Paystream is a peer-to-peer lending protocol on Solana that matches lenders and borrowers directly to eliminate the APY spread typical in pool-based lending platforms, enabling borrowers to pay lower rates and lenders to earn higher yields with zero idle capital. The host is skeptical about adoption, noting the project has only 36 daily active users and the product may still be in waitlist phase.

topics.text: Paystream unifies peer-to-peer lending, leveraged liquidity provision, and yield routing into a single capital-efficient engine on Solana.
Paystream eliminates the wide APY spread seen in pool-based models like Aave and Compound by matching lenders and borrowers directly.
On typical lending platforms, borrowers pay 15% and lenders earn 8%, but Paystream reduces borrowing rates to 11-12% through direct matching.
Paystream has only 36 daily active users according to a tweet the host references.
The host notes that Paystream is not highlighting user metrics on Twitter or their website, and the product may still be in waitlist phase rather than fully live.
The host identifies peer-to-peer lending as a potentially good on-chain margin trading business if Paystream demonstrates user adoption.

D7GXH-e2xfI.tldr: Fundle is a pre-Kickstarter launchpad that lets creators raise $20k–$50k in stablecoins (USDC) without launching tokens, positioning backers as lenders who receive repayment plus rewards if the creator succeeds on Kickstarter afterward. Founder Yaseph, a developer from Croatia, argues this model solves crypto's stigma problem for creators (especially artists) who reject tokens while giving backers tangible upside and early-access rewards; the platform has already funded an $8k animated comic in under an hour.

topics.text: Founder's background: 28-year-old technical founder from Croatia who began in crypto by developing for Remnants, a Web3 gaming platform, which demystified NFTs for him through direct user feedback.
Fundle uses stablecoins instead of tokens to onboard creators who hate crypto; backers interact with 'digital dollars' (USDC) not speculative assets, removing the stigma that killed NFT adoption.

Kickstarter limitation: only creators from 25 countries can raise there, and it cannot do revenue-share or reward early backers; Fundle's stablecoin model democratizes access globally and enables affiliate marketing.

Fundle operates as a peer-to-peer loan marketplace where creators borrow $20k–$50k pre-Kickstarter; if they reach Kickstarter and succeed, they repay backers a percentage of sales plus send physical/digital rewards.
Success so far: $800 internal test with 60 backers, then an $8k animated comic funded in under one hour with 70 backers, next a $20k crypto poker set campaign launching this week.

wP3vlCxE0vk.tldr: Uplift is a cross-platform command center for managing AI agents, built by RV (formerly homeless, now 27), who moved to San Francisco three months ago and is working with the Mercy/ICM.Run team to build a hacker house and event space. His story is remarkable: he was kicked out at 18, spent years in esports and various trades, and a community spontaneously launched an Uplift token on Raydium when his dog died during a competition, which he used as runway to move to SF and build the product.

topics.text: RV moved to San Francisco three months ago to work on Uplift, a cross-platform AI agent command center, after leaving esports and taking a plumbing job.
A token with ticker $UPLIFT was launched on Raydium by community members two days before RV's 18-year-old dog died, during a three-week competition, providing him runway to move to SF.
Uplift gives users one focal point to manage all their apps and AI agents, configure them online or offline, and store data locally and online.
RV has a technical co-founder with experience from a $15 million valued AI startup and another co-founder from Audit Brew, plus advisors in AI and robotics.
RV connected with Mercy and ICM.Run through X (Twitter), and is now helping host events in SF and planning to raise capital at Abu Dhabi conferences.
RV's main advice for Twitter success: get outside your comfort zone, engage in genuine DMs, build real human connections, and take initiative rather than just being a reply guy.
RV is working on raising capital in Q1 and launching Uplift's marketplace, with multiple job offers from SF startups and ongoing discussions about web3 initiatives.
RV plans to build an office hub in SF for web3 and web2 events, potentially a hacker house for content, programs, and hackathons, with nothing officially announced yet.
RV describes ICM.Run founders as the most down-to-earth people he's met in SF, the only time he felt welcome and at home since arriving, not judged or transactional.

yAFKE9KnPxY.tldr: LaunchOnSoar has launched a frequent flyer points program rewarding trading activity across Solanа platforms like Soar, Metadao, and Pump.fun, with points earned through holding, trading, and referrals; the host discusses how this mirrors Metadao's trajectory and highlights massive valuation arbitrage opportunities in projects like DFTV.

topics.text: Frequent flyer points program launched: participants claim initial points based on activity on Soar, Metadao, Believe, and Pump.fun.
Points earned through holding, trading, and referrals; 10% of points accrued by referrals are rewarded to the referrer.

7fA35LWd13w.tldr: AIMorphist is a voice-first AI workspace that aggregates access to multiple LLM models (GPT, Claude, Grok, etc.) in one local-first application, storing all conversations searchable and owned by the user rather than scattered across different platforms. Founders Norvous and Duke are launching the $MORPH token on SOAR imminently, with beta launching this week, and the most surprising element is their ambition to eventually enable agents with real agency—AI that can execute actions on your behalf with your credentials in a secure, private environment.

topics.text: Duke's background in cryptography and security; concern that users' conversations with AI are not owned by them but scattered across different platforms.
Privacy issue: when you use ChatGPT, all data goes through OpenAI's servers, they own it, and it's attached to your identity without full awareness from users.
Morphist is voice-first with push-to-talk interface using Motorola radio-style hold-to-speak and Telegram-style slide-to-lock, aggregating all LLM subscriptions into one searchable local workspace.
Users can switch between models mid-conversation and resubmit questions to multiple models simultaneously; threaded conversation tracking marks which model was used.

Backend infrastructure will route user information wherever they choose; future roadmap includes agentic AI with agents able to take action on user's behalf with their credentials in secure local environment.
Beta version launching this week; currently in alpha; mobile-first launch with desktop version planned; interactivity and syncing across platforms is a key milestone.

Duke co-drafted the first DID spec (decentralized identifiers) and founded Identic, a cryptographic identity protocol; users will be able to log in with Identic Key alongside Google sign-up at launch.
Morphist will use existing models initially via API at launch, but has partnerships in discussions for privacy-oriented models and plans to build their own agentic model for orchestration.
Monetization: flat subscription model giving access to all models; pricing still being modeled; may use allotment system like Cursor for different subscription tiers.
Token launching on SOAR within next few days; Soar chosen over Belief because of incentive alignment, availability, and willingness to help define narrative and ensure mutual success.

eo1Khtu570A.tldr: Secure Legion is a privacy-focused messaging app built on a novel "ping-pong" protocol that eliminates metadata exposure by using direct device-to-device communication with no servers or relays. Founder Eric, a former Navy Department of Defense developer, discusses how the app solves the core privacy problem that apps like WhatsApp and Signal claim to address but don't—preventing governments and corporations from accessing who you're talking to, when, and where.

topics.text: The ping-pong protocol: devices authenticate presence via a silent 'tap' signal, the recipient must manually authorize the message download, then an encrypted handshake occurs before the payload is sent.
Metadata is the real target: location, patterns of communication, and timing—not message content—are what governments and corporations actually care about.
Direct device-to-device messaging using Tor private clients eliminates the need for servers, relays, or exit nodes that other encrypted apps depend on.
The app is designed with no backdoors or information collection possible, and the entire source code is published on GitHub under a special license allowing non-commercial use.
Contact addition uses blockchain and IPFS: users receive a Contact ID and PIN, with encryption stored decentralized, preventing spam and unauthorized contact access.
Partnership with Perkins Fund to integrate file scanning for embedded malware and to add a payments feature similar to Apple Pay within the encrypted messaging threads.
Token utility includes pre-installed hardened Samsung phones sold with the app, with revenue going to buybacks and burns, plus three supported currencies: Solana, Zcash, and Secure Legion token.

Yk1DqBHIlno.tldr: DFTV is a 24/7 AI-powered broadcast news and entertainment channel for crypto and Web3, founded by Mark Evensky, a veteran media producer who worked on MTV News, CNET, and pioneered live streaming in the 1990s. The project raised under $2M previously and is now launching a $15M equity round after raising via Soore's DRP token standard; the most surprising aspect is its ambition to operate as a global alternative to CNBC and Fox Business with just under 50 employees, using AI to localize content in multiple languages and achieve 1/1000th the cost of traditional broadcast networks.

topics.text: Defiance Media aims to solve disinformation by combining blockchain, AI, and provenance to serve retail investors and consumers seeking credible information and entertainment for the next economy.

The founder has been live streaming since 1995 and created the first 24/7 streaming platform at pseudo.com in the mid-90s; participatory media with chat rooms is the defining difference from traditional broadcast.
DFTV has 80 million household reach via streaming television (connected TV, OTT, over-the-air) and plans to expand internationally with AI dubbing into Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic, and German.

Programming includes original shows like Reeve Collins specials, Defiance Daily with digital twin anchor Roxanna, and partnerships with conferences; contributors include Crypto Wendy, Bad Crypto Co, and Josh Krger's Edge.

Revenue model: content licensing (syndicated through Getty Editorial to 35,000 agencies), blockchain-verified licensing via Numbers Protocol, branded content partnerships, labs/enterprise solutions, marketplace, and membership—advertising is the smallest revenue line.
Chose Soore and the DRP standard for its participatory nature and curation philosophy, aligning with Defiance's approach to credible, curated content rather than wild west decentralized platforms.

Raised less than $2M from friends and family (including Tim Draper and others) through 2021-2024; planning $15M equity round in early 2025 at sub-$50M valuation, with 5% equity tied to Soore DRP token.
Team is less than 10 people across India, Philippines, Israel, and California; aspires to stay under 50 employees while operating at 1/1000th the cost of CNN (which has ~6,000 employees).
Upcoming programming includes a debate show in a boxing ring featuring Kevin O'Leary and Anthony Scaramucci, to be released early 2025 on Rumble.

Total addressable market includes 1+ billion people watching large screens globally; free ad-supported streaming TV is predicted to reach $64 billion in advertising within two years from current ~$25 billion.

CRF7qRqpVXg.tldr: Liminal Cash is a crypto-native neobank targeting international students, digital nomads, and cross-border money movers with free transfers and high-yield savings on blockchain infrastructure. Founded by a CTO with fintech banking background and a CEO from Crypto.com, the project launched its $LIL token on Pump and plans a major product launch in early 2025 after beta testing—the surprising element is their deliberate focus on retention over growth virality until the product achieves sustained user engagement.

topics.text: Founder's background: CTO previously at Fort Machine building core banking software for Lloyds, Curve, JP Morgan; CEO was a lawyer at Crypto.com and worked at Nosis Pay.
Nosis Pay was the first self-custodial debit card, tied to the Nosis ecosystem with ~3,000 users primarily in Europe, integrated with Monerium for stablecoin issuance.
$LIL token launched on Pump through Super Team UK hackathon recommendation without expectation of viral success.

Product targets international students, digital nomads, and international families with free cross-border transfers and multicurrency accounts—addressing pain points like Flywire's 6% tuition transfer fee.
Uses Morpho, Aave, and Caminno for high-yield savings APY, with user control over risk appetite selection.
Account abstraction via ERC-4337 protocol with Pimlo paymasters eliminates need for gas tokens on EVM chains.
Funding: $250k angel round from Nosis Pay and Crypto.com backers, Oxford seed fund backing, plus Pump farm revenue extending runway before seed round.

ICXaFdy6xzE.tldr: Spencer of Orgo discusses his AI agent infrastructure platform designed to automate computer-based tasks for enterprises. The founder separated from Believe following legal and structural considerations, raised funding from A16Z Scout and other investors, and is now targeting Series A/B startups for customer pilots starting in January, with claims that Anthropic's Opus model achieves 66% accuracy on benchmark tasks nearing human performance.

topics.text: Spencer separated Orgo from Believe due to legal considerations and structural differences; both teams realized they needed independent control over their respective projects.

A16Z Scout invested in Orgo approximately four weeks after the company's founding through a partner connection, with Scout fund scouts having individual budgets of a couple hundred thousand to identify emerging market opportunities.
Foreign Ventures joined as first investor for B2B enterprise network expertise; Corey Levy and Ben Pasnak joined as lead angels; Luke Whiting and Z Fellows also participated.
Anthropic's Opus model achieves 66% accuracy on state-of-the-art benchmarks, nearing 70% human performance, and can reliably complete 30 to 40 minute tasks with ongoing challenges in cost and speed.
Orgo targets Series A to Series B startups with 10-20 employees in insurance, healthcare, manufacturing, and logistics sectors for customer pilots beginning in January, not Fortune 500 enterprises.

Orgo differentiates from E2B (which focuses on code sandboxes) through 10x faster boot times at 500 milliseconds versus E2B's 5 seconds and 10x lower cost basis, with specialized focus purely on computer use.

Product roadmap includes Linux desktops with scalable RAM up to 128GB, multi-region support, Windows support now in pilot phase, with GPU compute planned for 2-3 months out due to lower current customer demand.

Enterprise deals under consideration involve 500,000 lifetime value customers running 500,000 virtual machines per month at 10-30 minute durations, generating approximately 100,000-150,000 annual revenue per customer.

50% of Orgo token supply is locked and vested over four years; 7.5% allocated to VC investors Corey Levy and Ben Pasnak; Spencer considering legal structures similar to Soar or Street for potential equity anchoring.

Spencer attended Z Fellows program and met with mentors who built 10+ billion dollar companies including founder of Zynga; planning Series A/seed-ish funding round in early spring with goal of securing one to three customers.

Cd8qCjVLjZE.tldr: Kyle, a Polymarket trader who's been active in prediction markets for under a year, discusses strategies for succeeding on Polymarket—the leading decentralized prediction platform. He highlights that most traders lack large wins, emphasizes the importance of finding your own edge rather than following others, and reveals that traders with apparent insider knowledge (like one who made $358K betting on Israel-Hamas ceasefire) may simply have superior research skills or luck; the most surprising insight is that prediction markets could eventually replace traditional news channels by pricing in information before it becomes public.

topics.text: Kyle's crypto journey started in 2022 with testnet farming, lost most of his bankroll during a meme season race, and moved to Polymarket prediction trading less than a year ago.
Kyle was 100% positioned for Andrew Cuomo to win New York mayor based on Trump and Elon Musk's endorsement, but lost that bet when Eric Adams (first Muslim mayor) won instead.
Kyle's four rules for Polymarket success: learn the platform, develop your own edge in markets you know, don't blindly follow other traders, and let the odds (collective wisdom) guide you.
Trader SB911 made $30K in November by trading Elon Musk-related markets and other sectors; his success depends heavily on Elon's Twitter activity and real-life events affecting Tesla and SpaceX.

Fusion One made a $358K profit by betting $60K-$55K on Israel-Hamas ceasefire by October 10-31 and $50K on US military action against Iran, demonstrating apparent insider edge or exceptional research.

Kyle's current trading focus is US politics and geopolitics with a 60% win rate; he avoids sports markets because outcomes are unpredictable, preferring tech and political sectors where analysis is more reliable.
Kyle's number one advice for beginners: never trade money you're afraid to lose, as prediction markets carry significant risk.
Kyle ran a public trading challenge from $50 to $5,000 two months ago but now keeps his main wallet private, believing public sharing reduces success chances.
Polymarket has the biggest liquidity of any prediction platform; other platforms like Limitless lack sufficient liquidity and are harder to use, making Polymarket the clear choice for traders.

BqPY6K0jhns.tldr: Pantheon, an analytics and trading terminal that started as a Believe ecosystem tool, is pivoting to become a proprietary AMM and liquidity provisioning infrastructure. The founder revealed that Believe is still secretly taking 30% of fees from projects that claim to have migrated away, a discovery made by analyzing wallet controls on Solana; Pantheon aims to compete with established players like Humidifi by claiming 3x better oracle efficiency.

topics.text: Believe app collapsed and the founder is unsure what to build next, exploring whether ICMs are finished as a category.
Pantheon started as analytics tool for Believe ecosystem but is now expanding to explore LP automation and AMM infrastructure on Meteora.
Believe is still collecting 30% of LP stake fees from every project that claims to have migrated, without disclosing this to builders.
Pantheon's business model shifted from ICM terminal to AMM and LP focus, with current burn rate covered by ad deals and paid listings.
The founder is building a proprietary AMM infrastructure with an oracle consuming 150 compute units versus Humidifi's 500, claiming 3x better efficiency.

bwZZ7XQwLUA.tldr: SurfCash is a fintech platform enabling nomads and travelers to pay rent and make payments in emerging markets via QR codes at 0.5% fees (6-10x cheaper than traditional methods). Founders Caesar (serial entrepreneur) and Akshad (21-year-old Solana veteran) are raising $250k through Star's launchpad, with the novel feature that governance and treasury decisions will be controlled by futarchy voting through Percent Markets, making it an "ownership token" rather than a traditional equity or governance token.

topics.text: Star launchpad is implementing new features: 1% of SurfCash's raise allocated to Star stakers and a referral program modeled on Hyperliquid's structure.
SurfCash charges 0.5% fees for stable coin to local QR code payments, compared to 10% in-store fees in Brazil and 2.5% for traditional card terminals.
Caesar previously founded Certify, which issued 1.5 million digital credentials impacting 800,000 people in Latin America, creating a user pipeline for SurfCash.
The product solves nomads paying cash rent in Southeast Asia: Akshad carried 500 cash bills to pay monthly rent in Vietnam and ATM fees cost 3% plus fixed charges.
SurfCash is live on Solana mobile and awaiting App Store approval to launch, targeting Vietnam's Danang digital nomad community first in partnership with SuperTeam.
Circle provided USDC grants, programmable wallet integration support, and co-marketing through their Alliance program over a one-year relationship.
SurfCash is raising $250k with 20% token allocation; governance via Percent Markets futarchy means a 25k monthly treasury allowance requiring holder votes for larger expenditures.
Future features include 15% APY staking, nomad insurance, co-working and hostel booking discounts, and yield generation on idle USDC through programmable wallets.
SurfCash plans expansion to Brazil (priority two), Argentina, and Colombia, targeting markets with unified QR code payment standards.

Dtn6JSSLEqk.tldr: EDEL is a DeFi lending platform for tokenized equities, founded by James, a former investment banker at Blomberg. The project has 40,000 waitlist signups and $1B in monthly transfer volume, and plans to launch testnet within the next week; the founder addresses Bubblemaps FUD by explaining their DEX launch mechanism and vesting structure were standard and transparent in documentation.

topics.text: Founder worked as sellside equity research analyst at Blomberg in London starting mid-2018, then founded Saxon as a market maker, prop fund, and validator.
EDEL's core infrastructure: borrow-lending for tokenized equities, DEX swaps, and planned super-app features including an EDEL card for spending assets.
Pull factor for users: ability to earn double yield by collecting both dividend yield and lending yield on tokenized equities, similar to wrapped staking.
40,000 users on waitlist; testnet rollout planned for end of next week with points program; full product launch timeline not yet specified.
Team includes seven tradfi-rooted staff, DeFi experts, and advisers from JP Morgan and Bank of America with securities lending market experience.
Revenue model: small percentage on yield/interest paid, liquidation margins with potential buyback program or yield return to token holders, plus ancillary services.
DEX launch used tax mechanism for first hour to prevent sniper bots, with 60% of token supply going to vesting contracts as stated in documentation.
Bubblemaps analysis was emotionally charged and missed obvious information in public docs; early sniper made half million to million dollars despite tax mechanism.
Crypto community needs to establish standard for acceptable token launches, distinguishing between VC launches that dump 90% and fair launches like pump.fun.

Abclfv5qERY.tldr: Maya from StreetFDN discusses the platform's Q1 launch as an equity standard (not a launchpad) using ERC-S tokens for real companies, emphasizing legal rigor and avoiding the pitfalls of tokenomics theater; the most striking claim is that crypto will have zero application to robotics at scale unless tokens are equity-backed, making ERC-S the only viable path for hardware companies to access crypto capital.

topics.text: StreetFDN targeting Q1 launch after market downturn and regulatory work delayed initial November timeline
Maya believes crypto ICM theater and approaches like buybacks make no sense compared to web2 venture standards
Robotics companies cannot integrate blockchain meaningfully unless using equity-anchored tokens like ERC-S because hardware has no intrinsic use for blockchain
ERC-S gives token holders limited control through board proposals and treasury governance, but founders retain operational control unlike MetaDAO's approach
StreetFDN does not charge volume fees and takes only advisory equity vesting four years, aligning incentives for long-term success over hype launches
Founders can tokenize as little as 1% of equity without fully embracing crypto, with platform recommending lower percentages initially and adding more as founders gain confidence
Solana's current toxicity from gambling-addicted momentum traders makes it unsuitable for web2 founders; Base partnership with Noise is preferred
ERC-S SPV audits confirm companies are not running away with money but never force full audits as competitors would gain harmful alpha
Kleed launching on StreetFDN in batch two after Avi Patel takes time to understand marketing approach for both crypto and traditional investors
Maya holds 2% CLEED in public wallet plus side holdings and four-year advisory agreement with Kleed company; sees crypto angle as Kleed's moat for user distribution

PQkWWatpAIw.tldr: Thomas Perkins, founder of the PCEF nonprofit, discusses THRT, a blockchain-based security token that puts AI training data in the public domain for peer review. He turned down a $2.7M acquisition offer, emphasizing his mission to provide free cybersecurity tools rather than profit; the project has burned 5.2M tokens and attracted 10,000 users in 2.5 months.

topics.text: Thomas Perkins is a reverse engineer who built a malware analysis engine called Malor, which he sold to Internet 2.0, and later created a neural network that powers Tracix.

A venture capital firm offered $2.67M to purchase the THRT token, underlying code, and Tracix; Perkins declined because he had previously sold a product for millions without receiving the money and wanted to maintain control.

Tracix.com offers free cybersecurity tools where users drag-and-drop files to receive a verdict (unknown, safe, or malicious) and can decrypt and view the AI training data that informed the classification.

The token utility is paying for file uploads and publishing to IPFS, with most fees burned and some going to a development treasury; 10,000 users have signed up in 2.5 months with roughly 60 uploads to the public domain.

Perkins has burned 5.2M of a planned 10M token burn, with 4M left to burn; he is releasing an SDK this week for integration into other products, with a partnership to embed Tracix into a messaging app for file scanning.

Tracix currently holds 45M samples totaling 4.7 terabytes of training data; it achieves 91.64% accuracy on Windows and Linux files but only 3% on PDFs, so Perkins does not release features until accuracy exceeds 90%.
Perkins released 'Nosex 402' two weeks ago, a more secure version of HTTP 402 that hashes data before sending and locks it to that hash to prevent client-side tampering, with no fees for use.

The roadmap includes SDK release, Phantom wallet login integration to replace early HTTP 402, holder verification for token-gated requests, IOC export for enterprise tools, and multi-file upload functionality.

7acI4jr9ZOI.tldr: Sanafi is an onchain neobank built on Solana that enables self-custody, borderless money, and DeFi access through a single app, targeting unbanked populations in Asia. Founders J and G, with prior experience at Coinbase and stablecoin companies, discuss their vision for a privacy-enabled money app with their own stablecoin (Sanafi USD) and sidechain launching later.

topics.text: Sanafi became 100% independent from Believe launchpad 48 hours before this interview and is now collaborating with Meteora.
In the Philippines, banks have access to customer funds and can freeze dormant accounts per government regulation, motivating Sanafi's self-custody solution.
Sanafi's TAM is estimated at $2-4 trillion on the bullish case for onchain money apps, with $7-10 trillion for the broader ethical finance market growing to $35-50 trillion by 2030.
Sanafi positions itself as Neobank 2.0, differentiating through privacy features, end-to-end onchain banking, DeFi integration, low fees, and gasless transactions.
The Sanafi virtual card, powered by Rain, lets users top up with stablecoins and earn Sanafi token rewards on spending.
Sanafi token serves as in-app currency, earned through card spending and referrals, required for premium AI features, and used for rewards distribution.

Sanafi's upcoming privacy features use ZK proofs and ZK-SNARKs through Nonce for confidential transactions and private swaps, making it the first onchain money app on Solana with native privacy transfers.
Sanafi Chain is already on testnet with 80 million transactions, and Sanafi USD stablecoin is being developed for next year as the app's default stablecoin.
Sanafi has been building for six to seven months in public via the internet capital markets narrative, while competing with established players like Alchemy.

klz1MroNYfo.tldr: Mercy from ICM.Run discusses how the DAO is expanding beyond incubating external projects into building its own protocols and capturing fee revenue for token holders. The founder explains their strategy to onboard Web2 tech founders by building trust through in-person events rather than pushing token launches, and reveals they're targeting $1 million per month in protocol fees distributed to ICM stakers.

topics.text: Founder.run partnership launching tours in New York and San Francisco, focusing on Solana-centric communities building public goods.
ICM.Run DAO traveled as a team of nine to San Francisco and hosted an event with 90-100 founders at the Dow Dun office.
The founder's strategy with Web2 founders is explicitly no onboarding: no wallet downloads, no convincing them crypto is superior, just conversations about their business and fundraising needs.
ICM.Run has a two-year runway without needing to financially incentivize token launches, allowing longer relationship-building instead of quick conversions.
ICM.Run generated $3.6 million in protocol fees from the ecosystem through adjacent launchpads and neo-banking protocols.
The DAO is now incubating its own protocols with founder mentors, including a tokenized equities launchpad and a merit-based launchpad comparable to Orca on Solana.

V2ObB6Bt2-A.tldr: LaunchOnSOAR is a platform enabling investment in startups worldwide using blockchain, with tokens backed by senior debt notes tied to company value rather than utility. CEO Tom discusses how their model prevents token holder rugs seen in cases like Vector/Tensor, while revealing a pipeline including an AI product with over 1 million users already.

topics.text: Soar's model uses senior debt structure where token holders receive a portion of acquisition proceeds: if a company sells for $100M and Soar holds 5% circulating supply, $5M passes back to distribute to token holders.
Soar has three launch levels: permissionless (anyone deploys), verified (KYB/KYC verification of founders and domain), and curated (in-depth DD with multiple founder meetings and TAM assessment).
CPT, the first curated launch, had 5% entering bonding curve and LP, plus 1% to market maker paired with USDC, totaling 6% actually tradable circulating supply.
Soar is implementing anti-sniper measures for upcoming launches and planning a VIP badge rollout next week tied to whitelist access for high-value projects.

Soar's pipeline includes an AI product with over 1 million users and a couple million dollars annual revenue, plus another AI product tokenizing for the first time whose closest crypto comp is a half-billion dollar token.
Platform vision includes building Soar-exclusive indices for project diversification, limit orders, and potentially options (calls and puts) rather than perpetual futures to avoid liquidation issues.

qKAH4riHWl8.tldr: MOBY is a Solana trading app and screener that launched three weeks ago and reached 40,000 users with a trending algorithm tracking smart wallets. CEO Matteas discusses the app's discovery technology, DCA tracking features, 55% average rewards back to community, and plans to become the top trading venue on Solana while pioneering the ICM (Integrated Community Model) with buybacks targeting to make the buyback wallet the top MOI holder.

topics.text: MOBY has two products: mobbyscreener.com (a deck screener competitor) and the MOI mobile app launched three weeks ago with a clean UI focused on token discovery and trading on Solana.
The discovery algorithm tracks the smartest wallets on-chain updated every second; a case study shows the 67 coin was ranked number one on trending at 50k market cap.
The global DCA tracker shows real-time DCA orders on Solana, helping traders decide whether to scale in slowly if there's scheduled sell pressure or to wait until a DCA completes.
MOBY reached 40,000 users in the first three weeks, with over 50% of new users invited by friends; the app is firmly in the top 10 Solana mobile apps by trading volume.
50% of MOBY's fees go to buybacks of the MOBY token; the founder's goal is to make the buyback wallet the top MOI holder when dashboards are released.
Recent buybacks have brought MOBY supply holdings to nearly 1%, up from the previously mentioned 0.5% stealthily bought back since the last appearance.
MOBY defines ICM as blending product with community by tying community skin-in-the-game directly to a revenue-generating product through a common asset.
Active users receive $50 worth of MOBY codes to give to friends; multiple users have hit the 100K threshold earning $800-$1,000 in MOBI through the multi-level referral system.
MOBY gives an average of 55% back to the community on every trade across cashback and referral rewards, the most generous of any mobile trading app.
The founder predicts the market will turn around in 2026 and expects on-chain trading volumes to 5x to 10x when it does.

2iEtEeKqna4.tldr: Pantheon is a 'success primitive' platform that launches creator indices—tokenized portfolios managed by influential figures like podcast hosts or analysts—to solve the problem of 40 million tokens competing for scarce capital and attention. The founder, who spent $1 million acquiring four gamers through traditional marketing, argues the real issue isn't launching tokens but making them succeed post-launch, and Pantheon addresses this by permanently tethering communities to projects through staking yield and supply-shrinking mechanisms.

topics.text: Founder's background: 2014 crypto entry, backed over 100 projects through Met Capital family fund, expertise in DeFi tokenomics and economic architecture.
Built Bigger Arcade to provide economic infrastructure for Web3 games, but spent $1 million on user acquisition to acquire only 4 real gamers, costing $250,000 per head.
Core problem: 40 million tokens exist with ~1 million more created weekly, causing capital and attention spread too thinly across projects; 99.998% failure rate.
Creator indices: brand new asset class letting creators like podcast hosts launch index tokens exposing communities to curated deal flow, replacing traditional launchpad model.

Index structure: 50% of raised funds go to token liquidity pool, 50% to liquid fund controlled by creator; separate vault receives vested tokens over 24 months distributed to community as non-dilutive yield.
Example: MCG creator index receives 1% of each promoted project's token supply, vested 24 months into vault; community holds MCG token, stakes it, receives yield from all vault holdings.
Valuation formula: baseline price-to-earnings using yield APR similar to DeFi platforms like Lido (65x earnings ratio); every $1 in vault should equal ~$30 in token FTV.

kWjRG370C7U.tldr: Pyth is a financial data oracle that provides real-time price feeds for crypto, equities, commodities, and forex across 100+ blockchains. Chief of Marketing Papito discusses Pyth's competitive advantage through first-party data from major trading firms like Jump Trading and Blue Ocean, and reveals the company is monetizing through Pyth Pro subscriptions ($5-10k/month) with 60% of revenues going to the DAO, marking a shift toward sustainable tokenomics.

topics.text: Pyth provides 1,600 live price feeds covering crypto, real-world assets including equities, gold, silver, forex, and economic data like cash GDP.

Pyth's genesis came from Jump Trading and other trading firms seeking to solve the oracle problem for on-chain markets, building a model where data publishers like CIBO, Virtue, Optiver are rewarded for providing data.

The market data business is a $50 billion industry growing 15-20% year-on-year; Pyth's differentiator is exclusive access to first-party data from major trading firms versus third-party aggregated data used by competitors.
Pyth is the exclusive partner of Blue Ocean, which has 98-99% market share in overnight US equities trading, enabling Pyth to provide 24/7 Tesla and other equity pricing that competitors cannot.
Pyth is pricing Tesla and other US equities 24/7 through its Blue Ocean partnership, while tokenized stock platforms like Backed and Opening Bell on Solana are emerging for on-chain equity trading.
Pyth powers prediction markets like Limitless with hourly BTC and ETH price predictions, and provides data to Kashi for its yes-no prediction market oracle needs.
Pyth Pro is a subscription service launching at $5-10k per month with 40% of revenue going to Duro Labs for infrastructure and 60% to the DAO for governance-decided allocation.
The PT token's current utility includes staking onto publishers to secure the network with 8% APY rewards paid each Thursday, plus governance rights.

Pyth was number one oracle by trading volume on DeFi Llama until that metric was removed; the company is now focused on monetization while continuing to expand asset coverage and blockchain deployments.

1KEKXvGqTZY.tldr: Cipher is an ultra-secure neo bank on Solana offering self-custody banking, payment cards, and a security layer called Proof of Cipher that scans websites for malicious activity. Founder Julian, a former hacker, discusses how the ecosystem protects users from wallet drains through partnerships with BitGo (insuring up to $250M), Hacken (auditor), and Chainalysis, while planning to tokenize company equity and launch a DMM for web2 companies to go on-chain by December.

topics.text: Proof of Cipher scans every interaction on a website and marks buttons as safe, malicious, or blocked, with all data recorded on Solana's proof of history.
Orbit Earn shares 15% of all profits from the complete Cipher ecosystem with token stakers, currently low volume but expected to scale with wallet and card launches.
Four card products planned: debit card for USDC/Solana/Cipher payments, membership card for gym and services, business card with accounting software integration, and a fourth undisclosed card.
The security extension and app work together; the extension blocks malicious websites entirely without showing warnings, while 90% of websites collect user data that the system protects against.
DMM launching in December targets web2 companies tokenizing equity and products in permission pools at 7.5% fees, half the rate of Meteora's 15-20%.
Cipher token represents profit-sharing through proof of stake and will be tokenized to represent company equity with heavy due diligence, separate from future buyback systems.
Cipher is raising venture capital to fund audits and development while maintaining founder ownership; currently only two people (Julian and Ricardo) with outsourced work.
BitGo partnership provides multi-signature vault custody with threshold controls; if funds are drained, Chainalysis partners to recover them, with BitGo insurance covering up to $250 million.

JsgtP-nXIkA.tldr: Solomon Labs is a composable stablecoin (USDV) that generates yield via basis trading strategies, with an ownership token (SOLO) launching on MetaDAO. Founder Ranga explains how Solomon differs from competitors like Aave's ENA by making the stablecoin itself productive through 'Yield as a Service' rather than requiring users to stake a separate token, targeting 15% APY while surviving extreme market events like the October 10th Binance dislocation.

topics.text: Solomon Labs approached MetaDAO about a month ago after the founder met the team at Solana Accelerate in New York in March or April.

MetaDAO's allocation mechanism: holders of any ownership coin (Avichi, Umbra, etc.) accumulate 1 point per dollar held per day, with allocation to new ICOs based on points rather than capital committed, and points decay by 1% daily.
Solomon Labs ran a private beta for six to seven months, distributed over $30,000 in real yield on $1.5 million TVL, and survived the October 10th Binance dislocations and auto-deleveraging events.

Founder Ranga's background: electrical and biomedical engineering, worked at BlackBerry/RIM, designed industrial protocols, founded Zywatt renewable energy project in 2017, built NFT lending protocol doing $30-40 million volume as anon in 2021-22.

USDV is the composable stablecoin staying at $1; sUSDV is the staked version earning permissionless yield; SOLO is the governance token representing ownership of the protocol's revenues via MetaDAO's treasury system.

Yield as a Service (YAS) allows USDV holders like LPs and neobanks to opt-in via one click to stream 15-16% yield directly without lockups or cooldowns, keeping the stablecoin composable for DEX pools and treasury holdings.

Solomon's basis trade strategy: long spot, short perpetuals on Binance, collecting funding rates with no directional market risk, historically generating 15% annualized yield; infrastructure built from scratch with Sephu custody provider and automated smart orders to avoid manual trading.

Raising $2 million for one-and-a-half to two years runway, targeting $5-8 million to scale; capital needed for USDC-USDV liquidity pools, reserves, better exchange rates from venues, and deploying into basis strategy to generate day-one revenue for treasury liquidity mining.

Neobank use case: users hold USDV through neobank debit cards and earn yield via YAS without cooldowns, avoiding the 7-day unlock periods of competing staked stablecoins that would require selling into illiquid DEX pools.

Third team member Stephen (former PayPal/PYUSD lead) hired after being introduced through Rocket Pool community connections; head of growth and business development establishing integrations across Solana and EOS DeFi protocols as day-one launch partners.

B9POoC1hWJo.tldr: Jake Gallen from Migrate Fund discusses how his platform enables crypto projects to move their liquidity pools between launchpads and AMMs—a service that emerged from necessity when his own project needed to rebrand. With over 200 teams in conversation and 16 completed migrations, Migrate Fund charges 3.75% of migrated liquidity and has generated ~$200k in revenue, positioning itself as the dominant player in a newly created market as competitors have stalled.

topics.text: Migrate Fund launched in July 2024 after initial backlash, addressing the inability for teams with locked liquidity pools to move their assets to other launchpads.
Migrate Fund charges a one-time fee of 3.75% of total liquidity migrated, with no upfront costs, perpetual fees, or token stakes taken from projects.
Zero's migration achieved 95% participation, with 97% of all possible tokens migrated, described as nearly impossible and unlikely to be surpassed.
The 'migration squeeze' occurs on the final day when 70%+ participation creates low float conditions, triggering 120-150% price pumps as speculators rush in before migration closes.

Believe's failed migration diluted supply by 30% and penalized all non-migrators, affecting both groups; Migrate Fund instead recommends penalizing only late migrators at 25-50% rates to preserve supply.
The upcoming Pump Fun migration group will feature over 20 teams migrating simultaneously, expected to generate significant attention and speculation similar to the September Raydium/Bonk group.

Migrate Fund operates as a neutral third party between competing launchpad ecosystems (Pump Fun, Bonk/Raydium, Meteora/Jupiter), taking no sides while launchpads bring business directly to the platform.

Projects typically migrate at two lifecycle stages: early-stage teams on last legs seeking ecosystem support, or 15-20M market cap projects seeking full LP control by moving to AMMs like Raydium or Meteora.

Q66DDI131Yo.tldr: AlgonFX is a forex trading algorithm that operates on-chain vaults and generates yield for its $ALG token holders through buybacks and reward distributions. Founder Winch discusses relaunching their Bybit copy trading vault with $320k AUM already, a 3-year track record of 24x personal returns on EUR/USD, and upcoming on-chain wallet integration that will unlock access for US and UK users currently restricted from their platform.

topics.text: Relaunched copy trading vault now has $320,000 total assets under management with consistent positive returns while crypto markets decline.
Historical performance on original vault shows 72% win rate over 3 years, using grid trading strategy that closes multiple positions with small losses offset by larger profits.
Plan to migrate $ALG token from Solana to Solana due to misalignment with Belief's vision; still negotiating with launchpads including Meteor and Pump.fun.
Token utility structure: 50% of buyback profits go to treasury, 50% distributed as holder rewards; token-gated vaults with different risk levels and APY coming post-migration.
Receiving 15% share of profits from Bybit copy trading vault, currently generating $6,000-$8,000 monthly revenue with existing $320k AUM.
Private client deposits range from $20k to $10 million, including one client with €1.3 million under management for 1.5 years.
EUR/USD pair trades ~$6 trillion daily volume with no market manipulation, providing predictability that crypto and stock markets lack.
Future plans include testing stock market algorithms starting tomorrow, on-chain wallet deployment to enable US and UK user access, and potential DeFi yield strategies within one year.

P7yMvoJDuCY.tldr: Loyal is building private AI on Solana where all conversations and transactions happen on-chain with cryptographic guarantees that user data can't be accessed or leaked. The founders, two AI researchers from physics and ad-tech backgrounds, just raised $2.5M via MetaDAO and are shipping Telegram handle-based payments this week—solving the problem that lawyers, traders, and VCs currently can't use ChatGPT for sensitive work without risking discovery in court or data breaches.

topics.text: Legal discovery risk: one IRS request can expose all ChatGPT conversations about taxes, tokens, and strategies—information protected if discussed with lawyers or therapists, but fully discoverable when processed by LLMs.

Big tech compliance: top four companies (Microsoft, Meta, Apple, Google) gave up data on 10 million users to governments in last 10 years, with requests growing 25% year-over-year and 35% from US alone.

Telegram integration: users can send payments by saying 'send 100 bucks to mom' and the system figures out her Telegram handle and sends the transaction—solving address copy-paste errors and eliminating the need to ask wallet addresses repeatedly.

On-chain architecture: every message, response, transaction, and conversation is facilitated on-chain through private rollups with hardware-verified code execution, so there's no single point of failure and users own all their data tied to their wallet.

Target customer: marketing and BD people who handle 300+ Telegram messages daily from multiple group chats, need to prioritize responses and book calls without risking sensitive information like trade secrets or partnership details in ChatGPT.

Hardware verification for enterprises: confidential VMs create cryptographic snapshots comparing deployed code against open-source GitHub code with hardware signatures, proving to compliance-heavy institutions that data cannot be extracted or saved.

A3YnGXKpPxw.tldr: RACER is a gamified trading game launching on Solana where players form racing teams backed by tokens, compete in hourly races based on market momentum, and earn RACER tokens and prize pools as rewards. Founder Jonathan discusses how the platform combines launchpad liquidity with Mario Party-style social gaming mechanics, with a tournament culminating in F1 and Breakpoint tickets to Abu Dhabi.

topics.text: Jonathan's background: six years in crypto, previously worked on Pirate Nation at Proof of Play and NFL Rivals at Mythical Games, co-founder Taylor built Dot on Base and Colts launchpad.

Core mechanic: players launch teams backed by coins, recruit RACER token holders to vote teams onto the track, top four teams compete in hourly races measured by market cap, volume, and price movement.
Two races daily: 12 p.m. Eastern and 7 p.m. Eastern, one hour each, with top three of four teams receiving prize pools split among team members and 10% to team owner.

Fuel points system: earned through daily check-ins, social activations, token holdings quests with partners like Jupiter and Meteora, and secret hint passcodes; spent on boosts that increase score multipliers during races.
Prize pool distribution: 50% of swap fees collected go to buy-and-burn RACER to squeeze supply; winning teams receive RACER tokens usable to vote teams back onto future tracks.
Visual presentation: four cars jockey on a track similar to Zed Run, with pop-up Mario Party-style mini-games appearing during the hour to let players earn additional points for their teams.
Team size: approximately four to five people including Taylor (CEO/founder), Jonathan (marketing), Bunny Kho Capital (marketing), and background developers.
Salana Grand Prix PFPs: available on Magic Eden, required to launch a team; grant 10% of prize pool to owner if team wins and bonus points based on rarity.

Launch timeline: RACER token goes live tomorrow (November 14) at 12 p.m. Eastern; first race begins at 7 p.m. Eastern; races run Thursday, Friday, then Monday through Friday, with weekends off for retooling.
Grand prize: top accumulator of RACER tokens over the seven-day tournament wins trip to Abu Dhabi for Breakpoint and F1 race with hotel and one guest included.

THTl5mQc3Zo.tldr: Xyber is a protocol for fair, verifiable AI agent launches and decentralized execution. Reus, a marketing manager for the anonymous collective, discusses their 0-to-100 engine (a sniping-proof launchpad alternative to bonding curves) and proof framework (which verifies AI logic on-chain using trusted execution environments). The most surprising element: they're building as an intentionally anonymous collective of 40+ engineers from Meta and Nvidia, open-sourcing everything while maintaining full transparency except for team identities.

topics.text: Xyber is a protocol for intelligent economies, building decentralized rails for AI agents and apps that can operate autonomously, including both digital and physical AI.
The 0-to-100 engine launches projects at zero market cap with everyone entering at the same price, preventing bonding curve manipulation and sniping through randomized trading start times.
The proof framework bridges off-chain AI logic with on-chain verification using trusted execution environments (TEEs), allowing verification of where data goes and how AI apps work.

Lumria is Xyber's first AI agent launched on the platform, with autonomous capabilities including tweeting on Twitter, streaming on YouTube, and running a community campaign with riddles that award XP.
Xyber integrated x42 for agent-to-agent payments without intermediaries, enabling AI agents to handle payments from users as part of their autonomous functionality.
Fundraising and token launch are planned for the near future, with details not yet publicly disclosed.
The team consists of 40+ members including tech leads, AI engineers, and developers from Meta and Nvidia, operating as an intentionally anonymous collective with fully open-sourced code.
The 0-to-500 engine smart contracts are 80-90% complete, with proof framework functionality rollout planned for the upcoming couple of months.
A $15,000 prize pool hackathon is running until November 17th, seeking AI agent concepts that could be built on Xyber, with submissions reviewed by the tech team.

DWpA5rJQfUU.tldr: ATM is a Solana and BNB trading platform launched on Pump Fun that helps retail traders discover and evaluate tokens through six algorithmic models, fake volume detection, and holder analytics. Founder Andrew discusses how the platform's year-old product achieved 1,500 paying customers and 35k total users before tokenizing last week, and reveals that 80% of trading success now depends on token discovery rather than exit strategy as 20,000 tokens launch daily on Pump Fun.

topics.text: ATM reports 72 tokens per day win rate, 82% accuracy, and average all-time high ROI of 190% when calculated to ATM holdings.
Pump Fun sees 20,000 token launches per day, forcing traders to spend 80% of effort on discovery rather than exit management.
Graph shows most Pump Fun tokens reach all-time high within the first 60 minutes; after one hour, almost none reach new peaks.
Volume checker tool detects fake volume by analyzing transaction instructions; 2% or less is organic, 2-10% is fake, over 10% is dangerous.
Six algorithms: five for Solana (starting at 200k market cap, expanding to 1M+) and one for BNB; additional holders analytics and prediction markets algorithm coming.
Team is 10 people including four developers; founder emphasizes data accuracy and clear communication as differentiation from existing analytics platforms.
Platform launched December 2023 as both Telegram and web products; token launched seven days ago after prioritizing product over marketing.
Profitable since second month; token fees shared with referrers and influencers; only revenue source from token is fees, not another separate product.
Prediction markets algorithm in research phase, combining onchain data with X social sentiment, expected in two to three months after testing.
Founder believes onchain is early in adoption cycle with 1-2 years of retail-friendly activity; bullish on both memecoins and prediction markets as core use cases.

AadApyNG2g8.tldr: Foundry's Unbrowse is an AI agent infrastructure that learns how websites work at the packet level rather than through UI clicking, enabling agents to access any web service via API calls. Founder Louis claims this approach is faster and more reliable than traditional computer use agents, with a token model that rewards indexers, websites, and token holders. The project is in beta with ~20 testers and aims to build a crowdsourced index of web abilities for AI agents.

topics.text: Unbrowse operates at the network packet layer instead of UI level, allowing agents to call APIs directly rather than clicking through web interfaces
Indexing is crowdsourced: users who browse websites teach the AI how to interact with them at the packet level, creating collective intelligence
Unbrowse integrates with MCP (Model Context Protocol), working with Claude, ChatGPT, or any AI agents to provide web access without code changes
Four-way payment split when agents use indexed abilities: indexer, website, investors (Foundry holders), and infrastructure each receive a portion, with investor portion burned or staked
Demo shows Unbrowse pulling inventory data in ~3 seconds versus 28 seconds for UI-based browser agents like Claude or Ellis
Foundry received Nvidia inception program backing with cloud credits from Google Cloud and AWS to handle compute costs
Currently in beta with approximately 20 testers; founder keeping user base limited to maintain first-mover advantage on the indexed abilities flywheel
Use case: agents can analyze web data like Google Trends and earnings reports to predict stock performance, as founder previously did manually
