The core product solves two problems: organizing chaotic X inboxes to track relationships and enable team access without sharing account passwords, and enabling outreach to find customers, partners, or podcast guests.
Mario Naffal and his team started using Inbox six to seven months ago, before the token launch three months ago, with the product achieving 20% month-over-month user growth.
Pricing is $49/month for starter plan or $79/month for pro plan; users can sign up at inboxapp.com, link their X account in 30 seconds, and invite team members with full message synchronization.
The pipeline feature lets teams track prospects through customizable statuses (cold lead, warm lead, customer) and send bulk messages to specific groups, with all columns and tags fully customizable.

Upcoming integrations with Instagram, LinkedIn, Telegram, and TikTok are planned; Instagram integration is straightforward due to team cooperation, while LinkedIn and TikTok present greater technical challenges.

Inbox is differentiated by being the first to combine multiple platforms in one tool, focus on team collaboration with shared message access, and the only X-focused DM management product at its scale.
The team is currently Kevin as product engineer, one additional engineer, and part-time support staff; they are hiring for a founding product engineer role paying $90,000-$160,000.

Product revenue funds all team salaries; the $50,000 USDC reward program distributes token fees to referrers and community members creating content or completing Discord tasks, running for 30 days with possibility of extension.

Upcoming AI features include customizable AI to answer messages faster, label conversations, and automate repetitive outreach work, plus integrations with Zapier and Make for notifications and CRM connections.

erGo382yexI.tldr: Moyai from $CODEC is building an SDK and infrastructure that simplifies robot training and deployment for developers, comparable to how Pump Fun simplified token launches. Muhammad, the founder, discusses their browser-based simulation tools, partnerships with Hugging Face and Chinese hardware manufacturers, and plans for a no-code marketplace where users can build, sell, and monetize robot skills using the $CODEC token as collateral.

topics.text: Muhammad is a 16-year developer from Algeria living in UAE, previously built a protocol on Starknet, now focused on AI and robotics infrastructure.
Moyai is considering partnerships with Chinese hardware manufacturers and factories, describing them as having the best advanced manufacturing in the world.
The team is self-funded with eight people, generating revenue from market makers and collected less than 60k from Pump Fun fees, reinvesting into liquidity pools.
Codec provides an SDK with tools for simulation management, inference, fine-tuning, and data collection that can be used directly from a browser without special hardware or dependencies.
The browser-based simulation environment is currently the only product like it on the market, allowing robot training in simulation without local GPU hardware.
Codec is in alpha and planning to release the first SDK version in October, with interest from Hugging Face's L-Robot project and other builders.
The $CODEC token will serve as collateral for creators listing operators on a marketplace; tokens are slashed if operators misbehave, and released back to creators over time if no issues occur.
Codec plans 3D-printable hardware for collecting GPS and motion sensor data to train robots, focusing on accessible and open-source sensor data collection.

UicB2HsZXdw.tldr: GRID is a unified trading platform aggregating prediction markets, crypto tokens, memes, and stocks into a single interface called the "money-making operating system." Founder Abe discusses the project's pivot from an infinite canvas to a focused trading terminal after poor initial reception, deflationary tokenomics with AI features, and cashback rewards for users.

topics.text: Founder previously worked on Staking.io, a Solana staking platform, and won first place in the Dallas track at Radar Hackathon for project Alpha FC.
GRID pivoted from an infinite canvas aggregating crypto products to a unified trading platform after poor product-market fit and community feedback.
The money-making operating system aggregates prediction markets from Koushi and Poly Market, CCM tokens, memecoins, Pokemon, and stocks all on one interface.
GRID uses Privy for wallet integration to allow users to move between Solana and Ethereum blockchains within one interface.
Real-time news feeds from crypto, CBS, Fox, MLB, NFL, Reddit, and Poly Market are integrated to show why assets are pumping.

tNhbaduYCOk.tldr: Memeputer is a platform enabling AI agents to autonomously manage meme coin communities through Twitter, Telegram bots, and token launches on Pump.fun and Axiom. Ben, a 20-year software veteran and founder of the acquired Stealth Test, built Memeputer after discovering agents could replace human community management—it's already burned 16% of its token supply and has seen a 4x pump since announcement.

topics.text: Founder's background: 20 years in software, built edtech platform with millions of users, been in crypto since Bitcoin, sold Stealth Test (NFT testing platform) to Hashlock in October 2023 for $15 million.
Memeputer origin: after building Banner Chefbot for Pump.fun users, Ben explored whether AI agents from infinite backrooms could autonomously decide and create meme coins like the Fartcoin meta.
Agent system: agents talk to each other riffing on trending tokens and topics, generating 48 random conversations per day, with users able to create their own agents and conversations.
Telegram integration bundles moderation, human verification, and buy bots into one white-labeled dashboard under an agent's personality, replacing the need for five separate bot services.
Token utility: deflationary model where 10% of launch rewards from coins created on the platform are burned; already burned over 16% of total supply; fair launch with no team allocations or vesting.

Content automation: structured tools let agents generate tweets in their voice, respond to pulled-in tweets from other accounts, and queue content without websocket automation (which would cost $43,000 monthly).

xRvK0RaX2kk.tldr: BlockSwap is a gamified trading platform built on Solana that lets users play rapid-fire prediction markets in 12-second rounds, described as "Guitar Hero meets Robinhood." Founder Joe Blau, who previously worked on Tesla's interface and at Amazon, explains that the platform generates revenue through a 1% fee on each vault of bets, and recently launched a $BLOXWAP token whose utility will be announced Monday—though the most striking claim is that Satoshi Nakamoto embedded a full gambling client in Bitcoin's original source code.

topics.text: Founder Joe Blau spent 7 years in government cryptography, worked on Tesla's on-screen interface, and worked at Amazon before starting BlockSwap.
BlockSwap is a gamified trading platform combining Guitar Hero and Robinhood mechanics, built on Solana, where users tap to trade in real-time prediction markets.
The founder claims Bitcoin's original source code contains a full-blown gambling client with betting and card-dealing functions, viewable in the GitHub repository.
The platform operates as a paramutual market where players bet against each other in PvP mode rather than against a market maker or house.
Revenue model: 1% fee taken from each vault of bets that closes out every 12 seconds, with multiple players generating more revenue opportunity.
A $BLOXWAP token launched recently with utility to be announced Monday, with the founder considering buybacks, distribution, or worker payments from platform fees.
The platform uses USDC as the base currency instead of the BlockSwap token to ensure new users immediately understand the value, as nobody recognizes the value of novel tokens.
The founder is excited about real-time prediction markets and stablecoins, and directs users to blockswap.com, @joeblau on X, and @blockswap for project updates.

6cDNECLzwK8.tldr: Phantom is a tokenized sports asset platform enabling athletes to raise capital by selling stakes in their future earnings, with founder Jonathan explaining how it works for tennis players, their new launchpad, and the $FANTC tennis-indexed token that uses creator fees to invest in selected players and buy back tokens.

topics.text: Founder's background: 13 years in tech, sold first company in 2019, then angel invested for two years before starting Phantom three years ago; also an LP in Sixman Ventures, early investor in Pump.

Tennis players need $500,000 to $1 million to fund their careers, primarily for coaching, travel, and support teams; Phantom enables them to raise $25,000 to $150,000 per year by tokenizing future prize money.

Investors receive 2% to 10% of a player's prize money once they reach top 150 ATP/WTA ranking; payback starts only after the player achieves this milestone, with typical 30% IRR and 4-5x multiple targeted.

Prize money is used instead of endorsement deals for payouts because it's highly predictable and publicly verifiable on ATP/WTA official sites, whereas endorsement deals are volatile and not public information.
Example: Chris Boyer raised $110,000 for 6.5% of prize money; currently ranked 120, has already earned over $500,000 this year and is in his second year of payback to investors.
Conservative scenario: if Chris Boyer stays ranked 150 through 2030, investors would still earn 11% IRR (1.1x return) on their investment.

KrTdbeBZMCA.tldr: PyroBuzz is an on-chain sponsorship platform for live streamers that lets users burn tokens to buy ad placements on creator streams, with protocol revenue flowing back to Pyro token holders via the Belief flywheel API. Founder Alex explains how the platform solves the lack of value accrual for creator tokens by connecting successful streamers to sustainable monetization.

topics.text: The core problem: creator tokens fade after launch even when streamers become successful, with no link between creator sponsorships and token value.
PyroBuzz integrates as an overlay using Restream or OBS, allowing streamers to display sponsors who burned the most tokens, with 30 active Pump Fun creators onboarded.
Sponsorship works by burning tokens to compete for banner ad placement on a creator's stream, replacing lower sponsors in real time.
Upcoming brand sponsorships feature will let non-crypto brands sponsor top streamers starting the following week after the conversation.
Pyro token holders receive protocol revenue through the Belief flywheel API, redirecting a portion of sponsor burn commissions to token holders.

Kn2OtJcP980.tldr: Avodot is a crypto portfolio management platform on Berachain offering AI trading agents, human-led portfolios, and indexes with crosschain functionality. Founder Paperhead discusses the V2 launch rolling out by October 3rd, a mobile app coming soon (65% of users already access via mobile), and Avonomics tokenomics featuring revenue-backed buybacks and burns targeting over 70% of revenue going to token acquisition and removal from circulation.

topics.text: Avodot is one of the leading projects on Berachain, offering a marketplace for portfolio management combining AI trading agents, human-led portfolios, and indexes.
The founder started as a developer and hacker from age 9, built and sold a startup, then created Avodot after recognizing Gen Z faces reduced financial opportunity compared to previous generations.
Avodot started as a Discord bot for copy trading on Ethereum, then evolved into a platform for AI trading agents and sophisticated portfolio management across multiple strategies.
V2 infrastructure introduces crosschain and chain-agnostic functionality allowing users to deposit USDC from Solana, Base, or other chains without managing separate wallets for each chain.
Trading is temporarily paused while the team calibrates for V2 launch happening on a rolling basis, with initial crosschain exposure infrastructure already built internally.
65% of Avodot users already access the platform on mobile, making a dedicated mobile app a priority launching in the next few weeks after V2 rollout completes October 3rd.

Avonomics tokenomics will use platform revenue to accumulate a team reserve first, then direct over 70% of subsequent revenue to revenue-backed token buybacks and burns, following a model similar to Hyperliquid and Pump.
Avodot is currently experiencing 50-60% month-over-month user growth with approximately 7,800 users, and expects this rate may moderate to 20-30% sustainably over the next three to six months.

URy4JPSbHto.tldr: PredictionSwap is a prediction market aggregator that consolidates fragmented markets across Polymarket, Koshi, and Limitless, letting users deploy capital to the best odds across platforms. Founder Jeff, a developer since 2017, built it after noticing prediction markets experiencing the same exponential growth DeFi saw in 2019, and the platform launches trading functionality next week with AI-powered market analysis.

topics.text: Jeff is the lead developer; he built a top-100 finance app from 2019-2022 before moving to prediction markets.
Prediction market volumes are taking off exponentially, similar to TVL growth in DeFi back in 2019.
PredictionSwap is a prediction market aggregator integrating the big three: Koshi (off-chain), Polymarket (Polygon), and Limitless (Base).
The platform has a news feed with verified stories that relate to different prediction markets, allowing users to snipe markets affected by breaking news.
PredictionSwap includes AI analysis powered by Perplexity and Grok that gives up-to-date data on markets.
Trading will launch on PredictionSwap next week as a full-blown trading terminal where users can deploy money directly without redirecting elsewhere.

PmGAyMuTTE8.tldr: Innovos, which makes sweat sensors for real-time hydration and electrolyte monitoring, announced a $15 million term sheet from GEM Token Fund and discussed partnerships with Garmin, Sony, Samsung, and major sports leagues. The founder revealed they're building a software app combining hydration data with sleep, stress, and other metrics for token holder utility.

topics.text: Discussions ongoing with MLS, WNBA, and major league hockey teams; some are testing the sensors for hydration and electrolyte monitoring in professional sports.
GEM Token Fund term sheet for $15 million, potentially combining equity and token, contingent on listing on a centralized exchange.
Sony interested in integrating sweat sensors into smartwatches; special fabric integration also planned as portfolio expansion.
App performing combined analysis of multiparameters: hydration combined with sleep, stress, heart rate variability, and steps to provide personalized conclusions.
Garmin integration in two phases: manual input launching in approximately one month, sensor usage integration targeting end of Q1 2026.
Token holders can use tokens to purchase premium subscription for access to complete AI analysis and combined health metrics.

TSJslPanmbk.tldr: Anthony presents Lens, a desktop crypto browser with a built-in non-custodial wallet that stores private keys in the operating system keychain instead of browser storage. The founder, who quit corporate work to enter crypto in late 2024, demonstrates how Lens lets users buy tokens in under a second directly from websites without logging in, claims the product is already profitable from transaction fees, and is seeking $2 million in funding at a $5 million valuation.

topics.text: Private keys stored in operating system keychain rather than browser storage, protected by hardware like T2 chip on Mac, avoiding Chrome extension vulnerabilities that have compromised wallets.
Lens is a bridge connecting artificial intelligence, the Solana blockchain, and the internet; built-in wallet enables instant transactions without Chrome extensions.
Comparison to Brave browser: Brave is a traditional browser with Chrome extensions, while Lens is built in Electron and offers deeper blockchain integration without supporting Chrome extensions.
Lens HUD feature auto-detects contract addresses in URLs and displays buy/sell actions; users can trade on Pump Fun without the website knowing they're there, eliminating front-running risk.
Private keys encrypted and exported as JSON file with user-set password, never touching clipboard; decryptor tool allows secure offline recovery without website access.
Lens automatically denies harmful website permissions including clipboard access, camera, video, and audio; only three npm dependencies used (Solana Web3, Google Firebase, one other).
Lens already profitable from transaction fees covering server infrastructure costs; founder seeking $2 million at $5 million valuation to hire developers, designers, and business development.

Founder owns 17% of Lens token unlocking 0.25% per week via Streamflow wallet; half of transaction fees automatically buy and burn tokens; committed not to sell tokens until market cap exceeds $2 million.
Vision analytics product launched separately; scans every holder of a token and their holdings to show top 100 common holdings; portions of Vision protocol revenue flow back to Lens.

siZ8uErRtiQ.tldr: Bob The Rebuilt, a PhD chemical engineer turned crypto researcher, argues that tokenized equity—not just buyback mechanisms—is essential for bringing institutional capital into crypto. He highlights Salutary as the leading project implementing legally enforceable control through tokens, allowing token holders to replace company leadership, and names NKP (a carbon credit company generating real revenue) and Kled as his top picks for true value creation on-chain.

topics.text: Kled is described as 'free money' because it raised at $40 million valuation with a fair value floor of $20 million, offering substantial downside protection compared to typical altcoins with zero base value.
Equity's value comes from control and authority over a company—the ability to hire, fire, and dictate direction—making it legally enforceable unlike crypto governance tokens.

Arbitrum's governance proposal to distribute 20 million ARB tokens for gaming dispersed funds loosely to people who gamed the system and sold, demonstrating that crypto governance is not legally enforceable.
Most profitable crypto investors operate cynically, believing dump-before-you-get-dumped-on is the only rule; true believers from 2021 are all dead or broke.
Institutions will not buy altcoins; only Bitcoin and some ETH attract serious money, so tokenized equity in real companies is needed to access institutional capital.

Salutary's framework ties token holders to legally enforceable control through a simple contract allowing them to vote no-confidence and seize company assets, IP, and treasury without requiring regulatory changes.
Buyback-only models fail because startups are unprofitable for years; a company like Uber would have done $0 in buybacks for 15 years, making the token worthless until profitability arrives.

Tokenizing private equity increases liquidity for founders and enables early exits at partial losses rather than zero or waiting for massive returns, attracting fund managers who currently avoid altcoins.

E9aA_DA3ehc.tldr: Ubie is building onchain AI agents that are verifiable, composable, and monetizable through an SDK, a custom RPC called Synapse, and a state layer for agent memory. Founder Alex, 19, discusses how agents can automate token launches and airdrops on Solana, and reveals the team recently doxxed, closed a partnership with Paya AI for agent-to-agent payments, and is registering as a real-world company in Sicily with plans for buybacks and ecosystem staking rewards.

topics.text: The Ubie team recently doxxed: Alex, Steve, Smile, Davorr, and Armorer, with a few contributors unable to dox for personal reasons.
Ubie makes AI agents first-class onchain entities through an SDK, state layer for onchain memory, Synapse RPC for infrastructure, and a visual dapp to deploy and monitor agents.

Synapse RPC is in closed beta with selective partners including Paya AI; UBI SDK and Synapse client SDK launching publicly in one to two days with a new bare metal server featuring 1.1 terabytes of RAM.

wKCilVEtv_Q.tldr: WuAI is a platform for creating AI agents on X that learn from your digital footprint and can reply to mentions on your behalf. David Rounders, the founder, explains that the team built this to work with the X API rather than web scraping, and the token has utility: 50% of credit purchases go to a vault for partnerships, while 50% flows to Heaven's flywheel.

topics.text: Founder's background: crypto user since 2017, data analyst, four-person team including CTO Bruno with European startup experience.
X API costs $200 monthly at entry level and $5,000 monthly at the tier WuAI uses, totaling roughly $60,000 annually.
Platform uses X API instead of web scraping, unlike competitors whose accounts got banned, to access tweets, mentions, follows, and likes.
Two main use cases: agents for crypto communities and personal agents that save time by replying to mentions automatically, with future validation step so users can modify and train responses.

P7rTA8MXAiE.tldr: TradeVala is a short-form social media app combining crypto trading with tipping and creator rewards. Founder Ratimus discusses the platform's "sparks" incentive system, VCM token, and strategy to capture the creator token market on Pump Fun by offering automated clip distribution, tax deductions for creators, and revenue-sharing with content taggers.

topics.text: Ratimus has been in crypto since 2012 and started building crypto projects in late 2020 after noticing discoverability and ease-of-use problems.
TradeVala earns users "sparks" points for posting, commenting, liking, swapping, and tipping; sparks are convertible to VCM token.

The app features a proprietary "island" on video feeds allowing users to tag and instantly buy digital assets; TradeVala charges 1% trading fees and shares 30% with creators or clippers who tag tokens.
Tipping feature required 5 months of Apple approval and makes TradeVala the only social crypto app with in-app short-form video tipping on the app store.
U.S. creators on TradeVala can claim $25,000 tax deduction for tips, which the founder identifies as a major marketing opportunity to recruit TikTok creators.
TradeVala is developing an automation suite for Pump Fun streamers to auto-clip their streams with tokens attached and post to TradeVala in real time.
Ratimus raised $500k from the community at $18 million valuation, self-funded for 3-4 months, and recently opened a seed round; VCM is the primary revenue play.
The founder emphasizes TradeVala as positioned to capture the creator token market where Pump Fun streamers' clips and content can be monetized and consumed on an ongoing basis.

oj43b_GW-2g.tldr: Tales of Meteora is a gamified MMO built on Moddio's game engine that wraps Meteor's DeFi tools (staking, liquidity pools) into an engaging multiplayer experience. The founder Aether discusses how the game lets token communities create towns with their own economies, earn yield through gameplay, and bring both web2 and web3 users into crypto—the surprising element being that 68 players locked tokens into a guild within hours of announcement, proving real demand for tokenized game mechanics.

topics.text: Moddio raised 495 Solana during whitelist phase with public launch opening in 28 minutes.
Moddio is a proprietary game engine built over eight or nine years specifically for massive multiplayer browser games with hundreds to thousands of simultaneous players.
Tales of Meteora is called gamified internet capital markets because it wraps DeFi mechanics like staking and liquidity pools into a game that onboards normies to crypto.
Land NFTs are coming soon and towns will be part of them, allowing players to own and customize towns with significant flexibility including building games like Mario Kart inside.
Players earn reputation points in each town by battling dungeons, leveling up, or completing quests, which unlock yield from that town's treasury made of liquidity pools and staking.
Every town can use its own token instead of TASM; about 20 partners including Mumu, Meteora, Jupiter, Send, and Xorg have already built towns with integrated tokens.
Guild membership requires locking tokens for 30 days to access quests; Bounty Town achieved 68 guild members within hours of announcement by requiring 100,000 bounty locked.
TASM holders will have future benefits including access to land NFTs and other unannounced features, with uses both inside and outside the game.
Characters themselves may become NFTs or have additional utility beyond being avatars, hinting at unnamed features in development.

JVO5uhSmiP4.tldr: Nathan, COO of Viva, discusses how the company transformed from a telco into a data company with an ad exchange that serves underbanked markets like Bolivia by accepting local currency payments and targeting local vendors with hyperlocal advertising powered by three layers of network data. The most striking element: Viva token holders could gain fractional royalty access to tokenized cell tower assets—potentially the first such real-world asset tokenization in the telecom industry.

topics.text: Global ad exchanges focus on USA, Canada, Europe, and Asia Pacific; 190+ other countries lumped into 'rest of world' category with substantially lower ARPU, leaving local advertisers in Bolivia sidelined by irrelevant global brands.

Viva integrated ad exchange directly into carrier core, accessing three data layers: app level (super app usage), device level (geolocation and device metrics), and network level (100% of packet flows, terabytes daily).

Viva is the only ad exchange accepting local currency (Bolivianos) for ad payments; will also accept Viva token as payment method, enabling local vendors to advertise without reliance on fluctuating fiat.

Company owns over 400 proprietary IPs across ad tech, AI, e-commerce, fintech, streaming, and telco systems with full-stack in-house software factory; vertical integration enables product launches in under two months versus industry standard of 6–18 months.

Phase 2 launch at Expo Cruceño in Santa Cruz, Bolivia will enable users to convert Bolivianos to cryptocurrency, buy Viva token or stablecoins on Solana, and pay bills; overcoming currency conversion as the biggest technical hurdle.

Employee token purchase program funded by ad exchange revenues will incentivize 1,000 employees as adoption ambassadors to train 30,000 points of sale on using Viva token; starting point for viral adoption in small, information-dense country.

Viva holds $1 billion in infrastructure including 10 data centers, 3 cores, and 1,400 towers; owns first-party data flowing through entire network, feeding proprietary AI and ML models for ad targeting and enterprise decision-making without licensing fees.

Tower tokenization model: traditional leaseback charges $1,000–$5,000 monthly on 30-year contracts; Viva pioneered RAN sharing technology offering revenue share on data throughput instead, enabling fractional royalty participation for token holders on tower assets.

Holdco partnering with major global carriers; Alva ecosystem will offer ad monetization and full product suite to other telcos with revenue share model, launching Q1 2025, with Viva holders receiving first notice of carrier partner announcements.

OzTOMKRwf2Y.tldr: FarmerJoe0x, a crypto trader and ICM advisor, discusses why Solana will outperform Ethereum this cycle, breaks down Pump Fun's $4B valuation as justified by its revenue and buyback program, and shares conviction picks including Meteora (bullish on $1B+ market cap), Bitcoin (core holding), and Fishwheel (micro-cap launchpad token). The most striking claim: he'd quit crypto if Meteora doesn't hit $1B within 45 days of trading.

topics.text: Pump Fun's $4 billion pre-sale valuation was warranted because the protocol generates $1 billion in revenue while buying back 100% of tokens, creating a compelling trade at lower market caps.
Pump Fun buying back 10 basis points of circulating supply daily means 1% of supply is repurchased every 10 days, offset 7% of $7 billion fully diluted supply already.
Treasury accumulation is superior to token burning for long-term projects because it preserves optionality for future incentives, airdrops, and community programs.
Fidgetals on Solana has the best TCG user experience despite lower volume than competitors Courtyard and Collector, with vault partnerships and live streaming pack features coming.
Solana is the institutional asset of this cycle because it's faster and easier to explain than Ethereum's 'programmable money'—it's a real-time operating system for money.
Meteora should reach $1 billion market cap within 45 days of trading because it does a third of Uniswap's volume with higher fees, implying $2–3 billion market cap conservatively.
Creator Capital Markets (ICM) require filtering for high-conviction holders over rotators; Ben Pasternack's belief in penalizing rotators mirrors VC practice of rewarding long-term conviction.
Robin Hood's upcoming social trading and copy-trading features will democratize access to micro-cap and crypto speculation, potentially flowing liquidity to Solana DEXes like Meteora.
Bitcoin should be a core holding for all crypto natives as digital gold with finite 21 million supply, superior to stacking depreciating USD or other inflation-hedging assets.
Fishwheel (FSH), the lead token on Token Mill launchpad, is a micro-cap bet that launchpad trading fees will pump its price, historically the winning trade on new launchpad platforms.

qvB_Q4W2JgQ.tldr: PMX is a Solana-native prediction market platform launching live where users can create markets (yes/no trades) as tradeable tokens, seed them with liquidity pre-sales, and earn creator fees. The founder Chris explains how it solves prediction market liquidity problems using Meteora's AMM instead of order books, making markets as easy to deploy as pump.fun coins—the surprising element is that market creators earn 1% of all fees regardless of which side wins, aligning incentives toward volume rather than outcome prediction.

topics.text: Chris explains prediction markets haven't been as easy as pump.fun because of infrastructure problems; PMX uses Meteora's AMM to solve liquidity issues by allowing dynamic liquidity provision.
Market creators get 1% of all trading fees from their market, incentivizing them to drive volume; a politics market doing 100 million in volume would generate $1 million in creator fees.
Pre-sales let anyone seed liquidity in USDC before a market launches; LPs who seed get their capital back at resolution plus a portion of LP fees based on their contribution.
Yes and no tokens get contract addresses (CAs) and trade on Jupiter, Axiom, and other DEXs just like meme coins, with current odds proportional to price.
Markets auto-resolve on a user-set date and pre-salers get their locked liquidity back even if no volume occurs, making it low-risk for market deployers.
Moderation is purely for market resolution based on criteria clarity; the team has 24/7 moderators; long-term plan includes community-based veto of moderators via UMA-style system.
Markets on PMX are Solana-native so no bridge fees to Polygon; Axiom UI provides better UX than PolyCmarket; creators get paid whenever their market is used, unlike PolyCmarket.
Polycule plans to add PMX trading to their Telegram bot and release X bots within a week; Moby Screener is creating a PMX section and already deploying two markets (NFL and memecoin).
Chris confirms one token policy—PQ token rebranding to PMX, not launching separate token; fees go partly to creators and partly to an assistance fund that benefits the token.

g9Q9lk3ga8I.tldr: HyperSwap is a cross-chain liquidity aggregator and bridge supporting 75+ blockchains with AI-powered routing, claiming subsecond swaps and top-1% speed and cost. Founder 0xSudoX, with 20 years in tech and 9 years in AI, discusses scaling to ecosystem apps like TipMyWallet and PALM while rolling out staking with 20% token buyback-and-burn against sell pressure.

topics.text: Founder spent 20 years in tech, started ~16 companies with 2 exits, joined Vodafone as UX designer in 2012 and became head of product innovation before leaving in 2020.
First exit: PollPluck, a data analytics company doing polls, surveys, and quizzes that pivoted from consumer to B2B and got acquired after 1.5 years.

W8E2PvOqa-8.tldr: Gavin, founder of Paragon, returns to discuss the $PRGN ecosystem's expansion beyond gaming into broader tech services. The project launched PTU points—a non-inflationary reward system for token holders—with live giveaways for gaming peripherals, secured 10.1k Microsoft Store installs in one month, and is pursuing Steam and Epic Games listings. Most surprising: Paragon is deliberately hiding crypto complexity to onboard non-crypto users, positioning itself as seamless consumer tech rather than a blockchain project.

topics.text: PTU points system live: holders earn points by holding Paragon and redeem them for entries in giveaways for gaming peripherals like Razer mice and ASUS monitors.
Microsoft Store approval: Paragon achieved 10.1k installs on Microsoft Store within one month, converting free users to paying customers.
Steam and Epic Games pursuit: applying for listings to build relationships and baseline awareness before PTU application full release.
PTU marketplace expansion: points will be redeemable for tournament entries, streamer collaborations, and competitive play, not tradeable for other crypto.
Revenue model for new verticals: 30-40% Paragon payment from partnerships like a PC warehouse scaling six figures annually, with 20% of purchases dedicated to token burns.
Hyper Swap integration coming: adding Bitcoin-to-Paragon swap option alongside existing Solana path to reduce friction for non-Solana crypto users.

fIHOdgQ9xvc.tldr: Adam, founder of Stardottfun (Star), discusses a live fundraising platform for startups launching token sales on stream. After raising $450K in seven days for Star itself, the platform's first live event with celebrity panelists and startups underperformed—four teams dropped out due to regulatory concerns, and the one team that did launch (Launch Labs) saw their token crash post-TGE, teaching the team critical lessons about vesting mechanics and investor alignment.

topics.text: Star is a live fundraising platform where startups launch public token sales on stream, combining Twitch, Kickstarter, and the NASDAQ.
Star's first fundraiser raised $450K in seven days, with the majority ($450K) coming in the final 12 hours after a 24/7 livestream of the founder pitching investors.
Fundraiser structure: 20% of token supply sold for minimum $250K and maximum $500K, with FTV calculated as a moving range, and remaining 80% going into 3–4 year vesting contracts.
Star's first live panel event had six teams confirmed but four dropped out one week before launch, citing regulatory concerns about unlicensed token sales being perceived as securities.
Launch Labs, the team that did pitch, raised $350K in one hour but experienced a chart collapse post-TGE due to pre-sale investors racing to exit immediately after token became claimable.
Vesting mechanism update: next launches will include investor vesting with 20% unlocked at TGE and 80% vesting, plus fee-sharing rewards to align incentives with price discovery.

Star uses a three-layer anti-scam system: AI model screening X and GitHub history, founder verification with green check marks, and manual TGE approval with ability to refund investors if project is illegitimate.
Star is building an 'intelligent buyback program' for teams, described as an innovation on current buyback methods that no other platform is doing.
Next event planned for September featuring crypto-native teams with established traction and revenue, plus three crypto-native funds as panelists actively looking for deal flow.

iPjJs8t8PIU.tldr: Amish founded Karma Wallet, an on-chain neo-bank that lets users send stablecoins directly to IBANs worldwide and receive money via virtual IBANs linked to their Solana wallets. The founder spent five years in e-commerce and drop-shipping, lost $50k to payment processor holds and chargebacks, then pivoted to crypto after launching a token on Solana that unexpectedly took off.

topics.text: Founded a sticker customization business at age 15, grew it to $30–50k monthly revenue within months using Facebook ads at $3 CPM in 2012.
Drop-shipping business reached $2.5 million in total revenue with 8–11% margins; lost $50k when supply chain failed on winter jackets and faced $15 chargebacks per refund.
Built a LinkedIn automation SaaS tool, then created Chatform (a Typeform clone in five days) before launching $KARMA token on Belief, which unexpectedly hit the bonding curve.
Analyzed on-chain data and concluded only fee-based businesses survive long-term in crypto; Axiom on Solana earns $1.8 million per day without a token.
Karma's first product: off-ramping USDC to any IBAN worldwide with live FX rates refreshed every 30 seconds; launched one week before the interview.
Users receive virtual IBANs linked to their Phantom wallets; incoming fiat automatically converts to crypto via Bridge partnership (acquired for $1 billion in January 2024).
171 total user signups with 35% KYC-verified; safety limits set at $10k per transaction and $100k per month, to be increased steadily.
Karma card launching in Q4 2024; fees from transfers, swaps, card spending, and merchant interchange will fund buybacks and inject real money on-chain.
Every transaction donates fees to charity decided by community; target audiences are e-commerce business owners seeking funds control and individual crypto holders.
Long-term vision: on-chain neo-bank with multiple products starting with ramping; detailed tokonomics and roadmap documentation releasing within days of the episode.

U28Kr-ocOnQ.tldr: AGOK is a no-code platform for creating AI agents using natural language prompts, recently launched on Solana with a token that pays for platform usage and votes on integration priorities. Founder Alex explains the platform lets non-technical users build customized AI assistants for business automation tasks without learning code or APIs, unlike competitors like Zapier or Crew.ai.

topics.text: The gap AGOK addresses: users couldn't create AI agents without learning terminal commands and coding, unlike tools like Eliza that required technical knowledge.
AGOK users create AI agents by writing a prompt, and another AI automatically creates and connects the agent's needed integrations in seconds.

Integrations are limited by what AGOK has built, with Google Mail and Calendar offering both basic (read-only) and full (write/send) capabilities; full integrations require user approval before autonomous actions.
A crypto user set up a whale watcher agent five days ago to monitor token transfers and internal wallet movements that don't appear on DexScreener.
Around one-third of all payments made with AGOK tokens and Stripe subscriptions will be used for token buybacks to support the ecosystem.

wKcbvnpFVrE.tldr: Winch founded Algon, a forex trading algorithm that turned a $10K deposit into $222K in under 3 years by analyzing EUR/USD market data and executing grid bot trades with 67-70% win rates through MetaTrader. The project tokenizes access via $ALG, with 50% of trading treasury profits going toward token buybacks, and Winch claims Bybit is preparing to make Algon an official broker partner within 2-3 months.

topics.text: Algon is a hedge fund trading algorithm for the forex market, specifically targeting the EUR/USD pair with 22x returns on a $10K deposit over 2 years 8 months.
The algorithm operates as a grid bot analyzing every bid, ask, volume, and order book wall to identify market patterns and execute roughly 10 trades per day with 67-70% win rates.
Copy trading on Bybit has generated $58.5K in AUM from 60 copy traders over 57 days, with 15% of profits feeding into the treasury for token buybacks.

The $ALG token flywheel: copy trading and client fees go into treasury, treasury profits are traded via the algorithm, and 50% of algorithm profits are used for token buybacks with the distribution method to be decided by token holder vote.

ngfoJuVNZDU.tldr: Spencer discusses Orgo, a platform providing isolated remote computers for AI agents to work on, enabling startups to spin up thousands of concurrent workers cheaply. He argues computer use—where AI can control computers like humans—will be as transformative as farming automation, potentially eliminating knowledge work jobs within two years, and positions Orgo as the infrastructure layer for the coming agent economy.

topics.text: Spencer has been programming for 12 years, started a web hosting company at 13, worked at JP Morgan on banking infrastructure, and spent the last two years focused on computer use—training AI models to look at screens and click to complete tasks.

Computer use agents can control computers like humans by viewing screenshots and executing clicks; current models cost roughly $8 per hour to run, with costs expected to drop 10x in the next several years as models improve.

Orgo provides remote, isolated virtual computers for AI agents instead of letting agents access users' personal computers; developers can spin up thousands of concurrent machines instantly and securely, scaling from 2 to 10,000+ concurrent instances.

Spencer believes within two years AI will have better average computer proficiency than humans, eliminating certain knowledge work jobs overnight similar to farming automation, though new jobs will emerge net-positive for humanity.

Orgo launched on Believe app two months ago after Spencer discussed ideas with founder Ben; the project received a grant from Believe after a successful launch and is now one of the top grant recipients on the platform.

Spencer is currently solo founder with contractors for design and engineering; he's hesitant to hire full W2 employees immediately, preferring to move quickly and focus on developer product-market fit before scaling the team.

Orgo has roughly 1,000 developers in public beta after a 50-person private beta one month ago; goal is 10,000 developers by year-end, and Spencer is already conducting user interviews with Fortune 100 companies without pursuing enterprise sales yet.

Spencer is not currently charging for Orgo; he tested a paywall initially but refunded users to gather feedback, and plans to charge production users running 10,000+ concurrent instances while keeping small developer tiers free.

Token utility rollout will happen in phases starting roughly one month out; Spencer aims to incentivize long-term holders with built-in value but acknowledges token buyers often differ from product users, making alignment non-trivial.

A hackathon participant built ephemeral crypto wallets for agents on Orgo, allowing agents to receive limited funds like $100 to transact online without access to the user's main bank account, demonstrating security applications.

r4Hl37ZycC4.tldr: Rainy is expanding beyond AI meme coin trading into prediction markets with Cloud9, an all-in-one AI terminal launching next week that automates trading through AI sniping, arbitrage, and copy trading. The founder claims they're the only company building custom AI models for both memes and prediction markets, and projects the space is still in early stages while his token has grown from 400k to 3 million in a month.

topics.text: Rainy is pivoting from meme prediction models to prediction markets, viewing both as applications of prediction AI.
Cloud9 is an all-in-one agentic terminal combining AI copy trading, AI arbitrage, and AI sniping for risk-free profit opportunities.
The AI sniper currently targets sports markets, using injury data and team information to execute trades before markets resolve based on news.
Cloud9 aggregates markets from Poly Market and Koshi, with the founder saying he's had contact with both platforms about integration.
Rainy claims to be the only company on earth using custom models for both memes and prediction markets.

Cloud9 beta launches next week, token-gated with pricing in the 3-4 million dollar range, though the founder is exploring credit card on-ramps through Hypersync partnership to onboard non-crypto users.
The founder states he worked with NASA PhDs and Nvidia engineers, and had early access to GPT-3 from OpenAI CTO Greg Brockman to apply AI to art.
RAIN token grew from 400k to 3 million market cap in approximately a month, with the founder attributing growth to first-mover status in custom AI models for prediction markets.

v7fTaFrC_mA.tldr: Johnny Fap, an on-chain trader and wallet analyst, shares his trading strategies for micro-cap coins on Solana, emphasizing capital preservation, day trading, and predicting liquidity flows. The most surprising insight: he sold all his Solana at $216 before the Trump/Melania coin launches—a move he credits as his best trade ever.

topics.text: Johnny's background: started crypto in 2017 buying Bitcoin at $4,000, round-tripped twice (2018 and 2019), lost money on Asuki NFT down 95%, and returned more focused in 2022.
Three key trading skills: capital preservation (number one), day trading (number two), and identifying best risk-reward setups by predicting where liquidity moves next.
Three-wallet setup: a Ledger for savings, a disconnected wallet for long-term holds without dopamine, and an Axiom-connected wallet for daily scalp trades.

Daily workflow: check Telegram groups for sentiment and coin calls in the morning, then review Dexscreener watch lists with price-level alerts, then monitor Twitter for key traders like Honey and Cryptosign for macro bias.
Twitter follows: only ~370 accounts followed, including three macro traders (Honey, Cryptosign, and one unnamed) whose bullish/bearish views dictate position size and profit-taking speed.

Solana vs. Ethereum: prefers Solana because of zero transaction costs and easy on-boarding via apps like Moonshot and FOMO, versus Ethereum's $500 swap fees and 5.5% token taxes during the 2021 bull run.

Top meme picks: Troll (main PumpFun meme with Alen Pan incentive to pump it), Do (down after 100k buy but good chart on higher timeframe), Gamble (fitting for PumpFun meta but ranging hard with risk of breakdown).
Trading card game meta: Pickle is a niche pick where one whale (Yuba Maidis) bought ~900 of ~2,000-3,000 cards, pushing the card price from $300 to $3k.
Pump entry at 880 million market cap during the sideways phase when everyone was bearish and calling Alen a scammer—signal that the bottom is in and volume could return.

BaruYl_Ksk0.tldr: Pierre from Collat discusses the launch of Collat V2, a real-world asset tokenization platform on Solana that enables trading of previously illiquid assets like real estate, startups, and collectibles with on-chain collateral backing. The most surprising element is that Collat is pursuing regulatory licenses (VASP, MiCA) and partnerships with traditional finance firms and audit companies like Deloitte to bridge crypto and traditional finance, positioning itself as infrastructure for "everything capital markets."

topics.text: Collat launched a token on pump.fun in early 2025 as a fair launch to bootstrap capital and create early adopter community.
Collat built a mobile app enabling purchase and sale of RWAs in seconds with simplified UX, including the example of getting his grandmother to buy USDY.
Collat's core strategy is ensuring tokenized assets have collateral secured on-chain, distinguishing them from memecoins and requiring audit firm verification.
Deloitte partnership involves initial platform audit and future goal of auditing bonded assets with proof-of-reserve, similar to USDC reserves.
Collat acquired VASP and MiCA (EU markets in crypto-assets) licenses as part of regulatory strategy to legitimize operations.
First asset launch: apartment units in a Paris building; issuer can structure yields through partners like RainFi or via buybacks.
RainFi partnership enables staking of COLLAT token and composable DeFi use cases where RWA tokens can be used for lending and borrowing.
Collat generates revenue through 5% migration fees on bonded assets, with 75% going to COLLAT token buybacks, plus trading fees.
Token utility: 100k COLLAT required to reach partner level and list assets on launchpad; future token flywheels to be unveiled.
V2 launches on the 10th with tens of assets ready, featuring automated liquidity pools, improved trading interface, and expanded asset classes beyond real estate.

GZ2ctwbgrXw.tldr: JP from MerkleHQ is building LetsLaunchXYZ, an ICM launchpad on Bonk Fund that focuses on onboarding profitable web2 businesses with real products rather than launching meme tokens. The founder discusses how his network and development studio capabilities differentiate the launchpad, and hints at a loyalty program model inspired by the Wrecked drinks brand.

topics.text: JP co-founded MerkleHQ, a Solana development studio, and worked on X Combinator, a culturally relevant DAO fund.
LetsLaunchXYZ is a product-first ICM launchpad with a loyalty program tied into it, inspired by the Wrecked drinks brand business model.

dlTZcQgqCao.tldr: Inbox_SOL (formerly TweetDM) is a CRM and X sales tool for managing direct messages and business outreach across platforms, founded by Kevin Picchi. The host discusses the product's security features, revenue-aligned tokenomics, and recent rebrand, with co-host Mercy highlighting it as essential infrastructure for web3 founders doing business development.

topics.text: Inbox rebranded from TweetDM two months ago to expand beyond X to Telegram and other platforms while maintaining focus on X throughout the year.

The platform organizes conversations into a unified inbox with team assignment, tagging, filtering by status (warm lead, reply needed), and a pipeline view showing contacts categorized as strangers, friends, or co-leads.

3SBMFxK_ixw.tldr: Razo Medici discusses AskSplat, an AI trading assistant, and its parent ecosystem ICM.Run, a DAO incubating ICM projects. The most striking claim: Splat is built by traders (not developers) across DeFi, NFT, and memecoin verticals specifically to give traders a 0.001% edge in real-time analysis, and the founder believes this positions it to become massive across multiple market cycles.

topics.text: AskSplat commissioned 101 unique 1-of-1 PFP artworks from an artist charging $200-300 each as a cultural timestamp of ICM era builders.
ICM.Run whitelisted every ICM trading community, reaching approximately 2,000 serious traders across fragmented ICM trading bases.
Splat's founding team consists of traders from different sectors: one from DeFi, one described as a top-five NFT trader, and Adam as a top memecoin trader of the last five years.
Splat provides real-time AI detection of new coins and can generate MCPs (multi-chain positioning), presented as a tool built by traders who understand traders need edge cases, not AI hype.

ICM.Run NFT PFPs will be rewarded when the DAO incubates projects, with the strategy being to only incubate 1% of submitted projects and reward the NFT holder community with liquidity and capital attention.
ICM.Run plans to build or incubate a Crunchbase-style platform to visualize and rank ICM coin value similarly to how TimeSwap visualizes different fund coins on-chain.

XGa9LlPUbwU.tldr: Fishcake from Believe Capital discusses their on-chain VC fund that backs Belief ecosystem projects like Hedgeimony, LaunchCoin, and AIXBC. The most surprising claim: they've supported more Belief project launches for free than the Belief team itself, and their fund has 2x'd since directly engaging with projects by taking transaction fees and reinvesting profits into token buybacks.

topics.text: Believe Capital runs a fund using transaction fees from their own token, has 2x'd the fund since getting hands-on with projects, buys back their token with trading profits, and maintains a whale community for 1% token holders.

Believe Capital's early investment in Hedgeimony when it was a few hundred thousand market cap, which has since become a top-5 Belief ecosystem project, hitting 7 million and now hovering around 5.7 million market cap.
One lead analyst on Believe Capital holds 4% of LaunchCoin, and the team is bullish on the project as part of their portfolio.

Believe Capital has multiple projects in pipeline waiting to launch, including one doing half a million ARR and another doing over a million ARR, both planning to convert fiat revenue to SOL and buy back their own tokens.

Believe Capital trades with a liquid fund using eight analysts including an engineer, ex-head of DeFi at Binance, and researchers skilled at detecting LARPs and grifts, sharing profits from exits with 50% to token buybacks and 50% back to the fund.

Hedgeimony curates 2500 news sources through an LLM to identify bullish or bearish signals for SOL price action in very short timeframes, executing up to 50x leverage positions on Hyperliquid lasting around 30 seconds.

LUE95QOmBX8.tldr: Nick Wenzel, driving across the country from California to Tennessee, joins the MCG podcast during the live ICM.Run public mint to discuss token utility for startups and his mentor role in the ICM ecosystem. The most striking claim: most startups launching tokens don't need them, and the biggest problem holding back ICM adoption is that token integrations are too convoluted for traders to understand the value proposition.

topics.text: Nick is relocating across the country and driving 33 hours total, currently in Tennessee going through the woods with intermittent service.
The ICM.Run DAO mentor program aims to bring together both web3 and web2 builders, with the goal of creating meaningful token integrations rather than meme coins for startups.
Token quality is identified as the main issue limiting ICM mindshare: traders aren't stupid, but convoluted token integrations make it unclear how tokens accrue value.
For a token to have value, it needs buy pressure from protocol revenue or product usage; examples cited are Hyperliquid's revenue-based model and Dupe's customer discount integration.
The ICM.Run public mint on Magic Eden filled completely within minutes, with floor price reaching 6 SOL after a 0.01 SOL Magic Eden fee.
Only 33 NFTs listed on secondary after the public mint completed, which the host interprets as evidence that botting was less severe than might be typical for such launches.
MCG and Meteorite Collective are distributing additional NFTs through giveaways to people who engage with the stream and to founders in the ecosystem who missed the public mint.

HogjZd5g3dY.tldr: KittyKunt, an early Chainlink investor and web2 founder with quarter-billion-dollar exits, discusses his role as a mentor and advisor at Meteora helping curate and guide ICM projects through launch. The most striking claim: he spearheaded BelieveApp's successful ICM ecosystem without taking public credit, and now wants to build an on-chain San Francisco where crypto founders collaborate and support each other like traditional tech hubs.

topics.text: KittyKunt got into Chainlink when it was in pennies and has always believed in utility-focused crypto projects.
He advises two ICM projects including TopG (TGE) and Soul Cipher, vetting founders on criteria like founder-market fit and long-term commitment rather than token price stability.
Meteora offered KittyKunt a role to run their ICM side as a pseudo-incubator, picking high-potential projects and providing guidance and resources to help them succeed.
KittyKunt wants to create a San Francisco-like culture on-chain where ICM founders chat with each other, discuss problems, and support each other's milestones.
He created a group chat with ICM founders, Soju, Vesper, and others on Telegram to facilitate collaboration and mutual support between projects.

hawHQP-_2-U.tldr: Royalarp and Dannyboycrypt0 from the Dow Fund team discuss launching ICM.run, a DAO incubator on their launchpad, featuring mentors like Luca Nets and backed by multiple high-profile crypto operators. The most striking revelation is that Dow Fund recently pivoted into building an agent platform (Goonfi) that has nothing to do with DAOs but is gaining traction by focusing on what people want: gambling and entertainment.

topics.text: ICM.run is launching on Dow Fund as a DAO incubator with a launch team handling daily issues; the founders describe it as having an unusually ambitious vision with highly capable operators.

The host notes ICM.run's team quality is unprecedented or the best in a very long time, with mentors like Luca Nets and heavy-hitting operators all aligned on the same goal of bringing people and companies on-chain.
Dow Fund's biggest lesson learned is getting basics right: building trust with people and ensuring they get the job done, with minimal platform changes needed for ICM.run's launch.
Dow Fund recently launched a Goonfi agent platform that has nothing to do with DAOs but is working because it focuses on what people actually want: gambling and entertainment.

The founder rejects launchpad competition mentality, arguing it's a zero-sum thinking problem; Dow Fund's tech is good enough that competitors are signing up, proving it's not about rivalry but fundamentals.

ICM.run plans to incubate value properly by creating treasury value through incubation rather than just capital swaps, making Dow Fund the fastest platform for their specific use case and risk appetite.

S2rmnXD6Nug.tldr: Indie.fund is a Web3 Kickstarter for indie games that has raised over $1M for developers, and its parent company is launching Tales of Meteora, a gamified capital markets MMO where different token communities own towns and dungeons, earn yield, and collaborate through quests. The co-founders discuss how this is the first time Web3 gaming has integrated yield and multi-token economies at scale, along with L4yuan's plans to incubate 30 ICM projects over six months through a DAO focused on community hackathons and tokenization infrastructure.

topics.text: Indie.fund described as Web3 Kickstarter enabling indie games to raise over $1M through token launches.
Tales of Meteora is a gamified internet capital markets MMO where token communities own towns and dungeons with their own tokens, and players earn yield.
Every tile on Tales of Meteora's world map will become a land NFT, with three types: wilds, towns, and dungeons that communities can own.
Quests system allows communities to collaborate: Meteora can partner with Xorg to create cross-town quests earning reputation points toward yield.

2Jl0-QqtlMI.tldr: StudholmeOne, an early ICO platform builder from 2017, is now working on ICM Run to democratize asset ownership through tokenized equity. The founder believes blockchain should enable decentralized ownership for everyday people rather than just serving as a technology solution, and is pioneering tokenized equity mechanics where projects can be acquired by token holders representing equity stakes.

topics.text: The founder built one of the first ICO platforms in the Netherlands in 2017 and has been in crypto since 2014, motivated by the 2008 recession and belief in decentralized ownership.
ICM Run differs from 2017 ICOs because it focuses on decentralized ownership of assets and democratized access for retail investors, rather than just blockchain technology hype.
The founder's previous token Matrix One (2021) had typical venture-backed tokenomics with exit liquidity, and he is now relaunching it with a fairer launch structure.
The founder has raised funding from Animoca Brands and DCG, and is exploring how to create fair tokenomics that give everyday investors early opportunities in projects.
Tokenizing equity allows projects to be acquired if someone purchases a certain amount of tokens representing equity, and enables benefits like loans against equity that pure tokens cannot offer.

UODx5_9UmsA.tldr: 0xPAH is an RWA launchpad built by Pierre that enables tokenization and trading of real-world assets like equity and collectibles on Solana through bonding curves, launching V2 in five days. Pierre discusses how he successfully navigated the Pump Fun era to launch Collat to a $90M market cap, and why he believes Solana is becoming the new NASDAQ for on-chain asset tokenization across multiple asset classes.

topics.text: Pierre was among the first 10,000 transactions on Collab and actively tracked utility coin launches during the Pump Fun ecosystem era.
Collat reached a $90 million market cap, launched in an era with no utility trader ecosystem or community spaces.
0xPAH built a mobile app enabling non-crypto-native users to buy and sell RWAs starting with one euro in seconds, including the founder's grandmother buying Onondo shares.
0xPAH built its own EDM-compatible layer one to simplify UX for RWA trading.

The RWA launchpad uses bonding curves to raise capital for real-world assets like Pokemon cards or equity, then acquires the collateral and enables trading of digital representations with DeFi liquidity.
Each asset class will require its own tokenomic structure, distribution strategy, collateral strategy, and community rather than one platform ruling all.
V2 of the launchpad launches in five days.

FxYhSIfuHEo.tldr: Miko, founder of Protokols, is joining ICM.run as a mentor to help web3 founders with product-led growth and organic user acquisition. He built tens of thousands of users without VC-funded marketing gimmicks, and will now guide incubated projects on scaling sustainably while the DAO itself aims to become a knowledge-sharing hub for the entire ecosystem, not just its direct participants.

topics.text: Miko was an early founder who tokenized his B2B and B2C dApp in 2022-2023, when the concept was heavily stigmatized.
Miko acquired tens of thousands of users through product-led viral campaigns, including Q1 and Q2 recap campaigns that generated around 15,000 cards without relying on VC-funded marketing shilling.
Miko joined ICM.run as the first mentor choice because he believes in helping founders navigate web3, which is a different game than traditional startup building.
Miko is already involved in the Belief app ecosystem on Ethereum and working with projects like Kruella to learn the incubator's network.
ICM.run's project selection works through mentors voting on application batches, aiming for roughly 70% unanimous consensus on teams to incubate.

The DAO's success will be measured not by the projects it incubates but by all projects that gain value from it without direct participation, modeled after Y Combinator's role as an ecosystem watering hole.

65x-FpMj5t4.tldr: Predict and Pump ($PNP) is a permissionless, AI-powered prediction market launchpad on Solana where anyone can create markets and earn 50% of fees. Frank, a developer on the team, explains how PNP uses LLMs for transparent settlement criteria, integrates multiple data sources to prevent oracle disputes, and plans to let users create markets directly from X posts—the most surprising element being their unusually creator-friendly fee split that captures just 15% for the platform itself.

topics.text: Revenue split: 1% market volume fee, 50% to market creators, 15% to PNP stakers, 15% to platform, remainder to referrals and insurance.
Founder rejected VC route due to loss of control and slow timelines; bootstrapped with team's own capital and benefited from Believe launchpad fees ($80k to date).
Team composition: 4 developers (lead dev Proxima), 3 community managers, 2 marketing specialists, plus outsourced legal team; registered as business in Panama.

Oracle transparency: settlement criteria publicly listed with sources (e.g., CoinMarketCap, CoinGecko); AI flags unresolvable markets before creation; users can create alternative markets with different resolution sources.

PNP is only prediction market enabling bets on specific altcoins reaching market caps (e.g., Troll hitting $100M); integrating DexScreener, YouTube data, and X data sources alongside existing Bird Eye and CoinMarketCap.
Growth metrics: ~100 markets created at initial launch, doubled to 200 markets within weeks; volume low relative to PolyMarket and Kalshi but team prioritizing marketing after product launch phase.

Fee structure: 1% on buy/sell transactions only (not on withdrawal); 50% to market creator, 50% split between team and holders; plans to adjust incentives for high-volume creators with higher fee percentages.

AJVFQB6YJPE.tldr: Web3Adam, who made $500,000 from MILF Coin and worked at Pudgy Penguins, is launching Splat, an AI-powered trading platform combining Trading View, Jupiter, and Hyperliquid with a chat interface for technical analysis. The platform charges 0.77% fees (down from 1%+ on competitors), with 100% of fees returned to users through buybacks, staking rewards, and point redemptions—and Adam claims he's pushing live this week.

topics.text: Adam made $500,000 from MILF Coin after turning $5,000 into $70,000 in a presale, then adding $20,000 more when minimum buy-ins increased to $10,000.

Adam worked at Pudgy Penguins for about a year starting early 2023, focusing on community and events; Luca Netz included mystery boxes from Cool Cats, DGods, and Nouns in Walmart toy boxes to promote the broader NFT ecosystem.
Splat launched through Meteora with a flat curve at 300K, meaning the price stays flat until 10,000 SOL of volume is filled, rather than using a bonding curve like Pump.fun.
Platform fees are 0.77% up and down on spot memcoins, 0.01% on Hyperliquid perpetuals; 50% of fees fund token buybacks, 40% go to stakers, 10% to point rewards.
Users earn points by trading on Splat; every season (month or two) points convert directly to SPLAT tokens, solving the problem that Photon points have no redemption path.
Splat's co-founder Eric is a top-tier NFT trader and broker who facilitated major sales including FTX's Board Apes; the third co-founder has crushed mining and NFTs since 2017.

jdWYjC_0kLM.tldr: Bobby, founder of Dupe, discusses AI shopping, competing with Amazon, and the evolution of ICM tokens tied to product network activity. He emphasizes that marketing is critical, reveals plans to target the $350M sponsorship space with sports teams, and explains how Dupe's new conversational commerce interface is already driving 50-60% more clicks to partners.

topics.text: Ben Pastranac started Believe with no crystallized vision, evolving from no direction to banning meme coin claims to now saying meme coins are dead—a normal startup trajectory similar to Facebook's gradual expansion.
75% of Dupe's growth is word-of-mouth; the other 25% is paid marketing through creators producing hundreds of videos daily, some reaching millions of views.
Bobby bought 1.1 million Believe tokens for Dupe's treasury to signal conviction that Believe will win the launchpad race and has the strongest brand.
Tokenized equity without actual legal equity is a scam risk; offshore entities like FTX's Bahamas setup make true token holder upside collection unreliable.

Dupe's token economics: no burning; instead, Bobby is accumulating 25% of supply in treasury by buying tokens from market using revenue from network activity like users inviting friends, clicking links, and shopping.

Dupe is shifting from furniture-only to broad shopping categories; 63% of ChatGPT users now shop on it, but 93% say ChatGPT doesn't fully address their needs, creating an opportunity for conversational commerce.
Dupe's new AI chat interface has driven 50-60% more clicks to partner sites in testing; Perplexity saw 5-6x shopping query growth and now 8 of 10 queries have shopping links.

Bobby's goal is 5 million monthly visitors by year-end (currently 2.3 million); he is in conversations with Premier League teams, with Manchester United's jersey sponsorship carrying a $350 million price tag.
Dupe is rebuilding its app from scratch, killing its 2,200-star binary to use Apple pre-install hacks to launch as the top app in the App Store on day one.
Bobby's definition of ICM: a financial primitive tying a token to product network activity—users generating revenue or engagement causes token appreciation, not equity.

C6ht9a4DYQg.tldr: Somo, a 20-year-old crypto trader and former startup founder, argues that Internet Capital Markets (ICM)—tokenized startups using open rails instead of gated VCs—represent a genuine regime shift, not just a narrative. He presents a framework for evaluating ICM projects using five criteria (market, timing, tokenomics, founder, chart) and discusses how long-form and short-form content strategies are critical to attracting retail buyers into the space.

topics.text: Somo's background: entered crypto during DeFi summer 2021, founded VFC DAO with 40-50 Middle Eastern researchers, worked as research intern at gaming guild learning game theory.
Built Longlist, a Crunchbase-for-crypto startup tracking VC funding rounds and accelerator graduates, shut down after a year despite paying customers because VCs don't deal-source through tools.

Internet Capital Markets defined as permissionless, borderless capital formation using tokens instead of equity and smart contracts instead of middlemen—described by Marc Andreessen as 'Linux for finance.'
ICM phases: ICO heaven (2017-18), VC heaven (high FTV low flow), memecoin era, and current regime shift combining legitimacy with digital markets enabled by regulatory support.

Tokenized startups flatten traditional funding stages (seed, angels, crowdfunding) into one token launch, allowing founders to raise, distribute ownership day one, and bootstrap community simultaneously.

Three pain points in ICM: regulation (two schools—catch-up clarity vs. tokens as new ownership shape), snipers (teams like Gavl and Muro working on solutions), and need for net new builders and investors.

Content virality strategy requires barbell approach: long-form deep content (podcasts, threads) to build belief in founders; short-form clips (TikTok, YouTube) to attract net new buyers; Mark Andreessen's concept applied.
Five evaluation buckets for ICM projects: market, timing, tokenomics, founder, chart—reframed from venture model of market/product/team to include liquidity and execution factors.

Somo's current positions: bullish on Flipper, Polymarket, prediction markets as regime that will persist; exited Football Fun at profit; believes prediction markets are foundational for ICM, not short-term narrative.

ktrph5SXzWU.tldr: WAM.fun is a social sentiment screener for Solana low-cap tokens that combines tweet volume, influencer activity, and behavioral analysis through an AI-powered WOM score to identify gems before mainstream attention. Founder Cru Kruella, a fintech and software engineer, built the platform to democratize sentiment analysis that Wall Street companies spend billions on, starting with Solana but eventually expanding to stocks and other speculative assets.

topics.text: Founder background: senior software engineer with fintech experience and two years of trading Solana low market caps, built WAM.fun to solve the gap between retail traders and institutional sentiment analysis.
WOM score is calculated using transformer models and machine learning to perform sentiment analysis on tweets, classifying them as bullish, neutral, or bearish to find bottoms rather than tops.

The leaderboard displays multiple behavioral metrics: tweet volume, influence (average follower count of discussers), emerging influence, unique sealers (accounts talking about the token), and price correlation with social activity.
Sealer Scan feature (in beta) allows searching Twitter handles to see all coins and tweets from that account, helping identify when big accounts or influencers discuss specific tokens.
Revenue model: 100% of 'get featured' sponsorship fees are used for buybacks and burns (currently burned 1% of supply), and 60% of 'submit token' submission fees go to buybacks.
User metrics: 1,000 average daily visitors, won the Material Collective hype award, team consists of four developers plus founder Cru Kruella working heads-down on feature development.
Upcoming portfolio sentiment analysis feature will let users input wallet addresses to analyze sentiment and behavioral patterns of their holdings without requiring wallet connections.

Long-term vision: establish WAM.fun on Solana, expand to other chains, then move into traditional markets including penny stocks and speculative assets; founder plans to publish academic paper on behavioral analysis model.

FVSdhpK8Lvs.tldr: Mercy presents ICM.Run, an incubator for Internet Capital Markets projects launching on Solana, which will tokenize 30 new projects (mostly first-time founders) and infrastructure alongside a DAO that gives early community members access to deal flow and airdrops. The conversation explores how tokenized startups represent a massive market opportunity as institutional capital remains sidelined from retail ICM trading, and how this could reshape finance over the next 6 years.

topics.text: Mercy walked away from his SAS company in March and helped friend Kevin launch Tweetm using product-led user acquisition strategies, which exceeded expectations and led to the broader ICM.Run vision.

ICM is defined as a utility company with revenue and a coin with a flywheel on a public ledger; institutional ICM from 2017-2023 (legacy utility coins with institutional investors) is now completely sidelined as retail trades the new on-chain version.

ICM.Run will incubate 30 projects (80% new tokenizing teams, 20% infrastructure); the DAO will accumulate 1-5% of each project's supply, with governance votes at 6 months to liquidate or continue, potentially launching a syndicated VC firm afterward.

The founder envisions a non-KYC platform where any group can form a DAO and make investments into early-stage ICM teams based on historical performance, with thousands of ICM.Run spin-offs eventually existing.

A free NFT mint (date TBD, aiming end of week) will whitelist early community members; 80%+ of supply is whitelisted to OG supporters and traders, with 20% public supply; NFT holders get airdrops and claims from incubated projects.

Mercy's mentor Stoome is leading relationships with two web2 hedge funds discussing tokenizing their startup portfolios; the legal framework is nearly complete and autonomous has joined as a contributor to write tokenized equity rules.

Mercy is bullish on AI-enabled rapid product development disrupting SaaS companies and creating opportunities for tokenized startups, citing how coding tools now allow anyone to build apps overnight that could compete with legacy software companies.

Institutional VCs' employees are actively trading ICM tokens with positions of 400k+ casually across multiple coins because institutional capital has been sidelined; institutions would deploy much more if legal pathways existed for non-KYC tokenized equity.

Every ICM.Run incubated project will ship with full documentation before launch; Mercy wants to avoid repeating early mistakes like Cled's lack of clarity and ensure professional token launches that don't get sniped in the first three candles.

Mercy believes this is a 6-year bet and a potential trade of a lifetime similar to how people got ahead of AI in 2022-2023; the vision includes brands like History Channel potentially tokenizing on this infrastructure in the future.

Tp7eb_EYABg.tldr: Gavin from Paragon discusses the PC optimization and gaming utility business's evolution into an ICM (Internet Capital Markets) project with token integration. The founder reveals they're redesigning their website to integrate instant swaps and a points redemption system for gaming hardware giveaways, have already burned 2% of supply in 46 days through revenue, and project 10x revenue growth in three months as they prepare a hard launch after accumulating 47,000 downloads across Microsoft Store and Epic Games.

topics.text: Website redesign includes instant swap functionality, wallet creation on-site, and integration of PTU points system redeemable for gaming hardware giveaways including full PCs, monitors, mice, and keyboards.

Paragon's core utility: holding PRGN tokens earns points redeemable for gaming gear, with different tier rewards for small holders versus whales, no other project offering this type of tangible hardware incentive.

Business metrics show evolution from pre-token revenue of 600-700k annually to current 700-800k post-token launch, with 47,000 total downloads across Microsoft Store and Epic Games, and trajectory to 10x revenue within three months.
Paragon customers receive 3x value discount when paying with PRGN tokens instead of fiat, driving token burns and creating the core business-to-token value loop.

Free Performance V4 application generates 74,000 YouTube views in one video alone, with 20,000-30,000 total downloads, creating massive upper-funnel awareness for paid PTU utility launching across Microsoft, Epic, and potentially Steam and Google Play Store.
Paragon became first crypto token-based company listed on Microsoft Store in four days due to founder's relationship with a Microsoft partner, compared to typical 3-4 week verification processes.

M6xIpdqlyAE.tldr: Quanto is a leverage trading exchange where users can deposit any asset from their wallet—NFTs, altcoins, meme coins—as collateral to trade perpetuals on pairs unavailable elsewhere. Founder YQ explains the controversial buyback flywheel: liquidations in non-Quanto collateral are sold on-chain to buy back QTO tokens (100% for liquidations, 70% of fees), while winners are paid in QTO, creating a mechanism where retail losses auto-generate token buybacks. The surprising claim: despite $2M in buybacks in the first month, only 1.6% of token supply has actually burned.

topics.text: Core product: users deposit illiquid assets like Board Apes or Chainlink as collateral to trade leverage on any pair, not just stablecoins.

Liquidation and debt mechanism: if a trader loses, they accrue QTO debt; if QTO price rises enough that debt exceeds collateral value, the collateral is liquidated and 100% of proceeds buy back QTO tokens.
Fee structure: 70% of trading fees are burned, 30% go to QLP (Quanto Liquidity Provider) stakers; liquidations are separate and all go to QLP, not to the team.
Token supply: 20% team with 1-year cliff and 1-year vest, 40% treasury for future incentives (currently unallocated), 14% cold wallet for withdrawals, remainder circulating.
YQ's background: traded perps for 5 years, wrote DeFi analysis, worked at VC as head of research, then took over the failed Ox protocol and rebuilt it as Quanto with a new team.

User growth strategy: deliberately slow-rolled marketing for the first month to fix bugs and clarify mechanisms; volume claims from late July were inflated due to QLP self-trading data collection errors, actual daily volume ~30-70M.
LTV (loan-to-value) ratios by asset: QTO and USDT at 1.0 (100%), BTC/ETH at 0.95, meme coins at 0.5–0.9 depending on market cap, visible on the homepage.
