YQ's current trading: went 200x short SOL and ETH yesterday, closed profitably; also shorted Hype thinking it would underperform but was wrong; uses the platform himself for all trading.
Burn rate: 2M tokens in buybacks in first 14 days, total 1.63% of circulating supply burned to date (~60M tokens), burn pace slowed from 6% in first week to 0.1–0.3% per week thereafter.

RxsRk5I8fIk.tldr: Starseed is an all-in-one trading dashboard for Solana that unifies charts, token screeners, wallet tools, and liquidity provision into customizable widgets. The founder Batman and team discuss their ScaleOut feature, which lets traders sell tokens as concentrated liquidity in price bins to reduce chart dump impact and collect fees—essentially functioning like limit orders that generate LP income. Upcoming automation tools like take-profit and stop-loss will be their next major push.

topics.text: Starseed evolved from an AI Discord bot recommending top Meteora pools in December 2024 to a full trading platform dashboard after the Alliance DAO hackathon in January.

ScaleOut feature: traders can concentrate liquidity at specific price bins and collect fees when buyers route through their pool, functioning like limit orders but generating LP income instead of just market sells.
Fee model: 0.004 SOL per position open/close (reduced for token holders), plus 2.5% cut of claimed LP fees; token holders with 10M SEED tokens pay 0% fees.
Daily active users: 740 in the past three days, defined as users performing actual transactions like opening, closing, or monitoring positions.
Upcoming automation features will include take-profit, stop-loss, and swapless rebalancing to move out-of-range liquidity to current price without incurring swap slippage.
Widget-based system allows future integrations with other projects; currently exploring perpetuals monitoring and considering Hyper EVM or enhanced Jupiter perps API.
Marketing strategy targets high-holder, high-market-cap communities like Uranus, positioning ScaleOut as a 'don't dump the chart' liquidity-provision alternative.
Star Seed Academy launches tomorrow at 10:00 a.m. EST covering Meteora fundamentals, bin mechanics, and step-by-step platform setup for new and experienced users.

oHAQqLYKqBc.tldr: Rainmaker is an AI trading agent platform on Solana that uses machine learning to predict which tokens will graduate (reach bonding curve completion) and automatically executes trades for users. Founder Rainey, who previously worked on AI projects with Nvidia, charges a 2% transaction fee and plans to use 50% of revenue for token buybacks; the platform is currently rolling out "Storm" agents to top holders with a bug fix pending.

topics.text: Founder previously founded one of the biggest web3 companies, collaborated with Nvidia on AI, and worked with NASA PhDs on new types of AI.
The model trained on two million token snapshots daily, predicting whether tokens will graduate with a single label: can this token graduate before it does.
Storm is an autonomous agent using the graduation prediction model at 90-98% confidence to automatically execute trades without user intervention.
2% transaction fee on all trades regardless of Rain token holdings; 50% of transaction fee revenue goes to token buybacks, with potential sliding fees based on trade performance.
Clone detection filters tokens by unique Twitter ID; the model examines engagement metrics and engagement timeframe on tweets to predict success.
Currently limiting Storm access to 100 users in the first week, scaling to 1,000 users long-term to test effects of coordinated trading on micro-cap tokens.
Founder owns approximately 3% of token supply; most holders are cold holders with larger stakes; team does not hold significant supply.
Received Meteorite Collective utility award grant and marketing support after initial grant application was unsuccessful.
Planning to ship new AI models every four to five days using daily data; future vision includes passive income Storm agents on Solana debit cards with cash back features.
Founder argues AI trading agents are necessary competitive advantage because private institutions already use AI models printing $100 million monthly on-chain for arbitrage.

6yBx3JlmrQg.tldr: Outlast App is a male wellness app using edging techniques to help users overcome porn addiction and premature ejaculation, founded by someone who built the product for himself. The founder describes an explosive launch reaching $2M market cap with $10K monthly revenue, now integrating an 'edge-to-earn' token system where users earn XP points redeemable for tokens, with buybacks funded by a percentage of app revenue.

topics.text: The app launched with viral momentum through Joseph Consumer Club, reaching $2 million market cap before experiencing a correction due to sniping.
Outlast is an edging app designed to help users overcome porn addiction and premature ejaculation by retraining the brain through progressive arousal control.
The app generated $10K revenue in the first two months, uses a freemium model with $30 annual subscription after a seven-day free trial, and currently has approximately 3,000 paying users.
The app features a six-week progression plan with modules, lessons, and challenges like '30 days no porn' that award XP points convertible to edge tokens.
Edge-to-earn model involves users earning XP through app usage, with platform revenue buybacks and token burns funding value capture.
The founder plans to expand the app's vision to include a female version and broader sexual intimacy education for couples, potentially doubling market reach.
The company is integrating peer-reviewed articles to back the science behind the app and is in conversations with thought leaders to legitimize the product.
The founder is considering future physical product lines such as natural condoms and organic lubricants as revenue scaling opportunities.

59sU_69N5f0.tldr: Luca, founder of JTVO, a decentralized AI inference platform built on Solana, discusses how the project grew organically to $7M in market cap through Asian markets within weeks of launch in April 2025. The founder reveals a novel equity model where investors allocate 30% of their investment capital directly to token liquidity while retaining 100% equity, and plans to launch distributed GPU mining in Q4 2025 where users contribute computing power in exchange for JTVO tokens.

topics.text: Founder Luca has a chemical engineering background and quit crypto in January 2025 when Trump and Melania peaked, then pivoted to AI.

JTVO launched in April 2025 after three days of preparation; first day generated $20k in fees, reached $100k market cap in seven days organically, then $7M through Korean and Chinese community outreach.

JTVO is a decentralized inference platform where users access multiple open-source AI models (Meta Llama, DeepSeek, Llama, GLM, Grok) with response speeds of 1,000 tokens per second in multiple languages.

The company operates multiple revenue streams: site builder, AI consulting and training, API services, and specialized products like bio/protein research tools; currently generating $6k per month across all products.
Founder spent approximately $30k on GPU infrastructure from Nvidia and is inspired by Render token's model of decentralized computing power.
Platform users already pay in USDC or Solana via Helopay and Solana Pay integration; fees collected are used for token buybacks.
Majority of early JTVO holders are from China and Korea with smaller Western cohort; founder maintains a separate 4,000-member Indonesian memecoin Telegram community.

ppxl9nnwNqc.tldr: Yara AI Systems is building a voice AI agent for crypto, allowing users to do market research, on-chain research, and execute trades by speaking to an interface. The founder discusses how the project launched four months ago on Moonshot, prioritized building an early beta over hype, and plans to generate revenue through usage-based fees paid in Solana with buybacks funding token burns.

topics.text: The team has 35+ years combined experience in full-stack engineering and consumer app marketing, currently three people plus contractors.
Yara uses EARS, an extensible framework for rapid deployment of integrations across multiple blockchains, with on-chain execution initially focused on Solana.
Yara Pro is a B2B offering allowing other web3 projects to deploy custom-trained conversational AI assistants for their communities.
The token launched four months ago on Moonshot; the team prioritized launching an early access beta over marketing hype to build a core community first.
Users interact with Yara by holding down the space bar to speak into a web interface that supports conversational AI, with mobile apps coming later.
Token burning is tied to LP volume: all Yara rewards get burned while Sol rewards go to the dev wallet for daily token buybacks, currently burning $25-$100 per day.
Future revenue model will use usage-based fees paid in Solana, with a percentage redirected to token buybacks alongside the existing burn mechanism.

f1xoIVXZqlc.tldr: Slash is a Chrome extension that acts as a browser-based AI agent, answering questions about any webpage and automating tasks like filling forms or navigating settings—essentially ChatGPT for the browser. Founder Peter discusses the recent Slash 2.0 pivot to closed beta with 60 weekly active users, the launch of Slash Pro/Enterprise subscriptions tomorrow, and the ambitious vision to build universal personal AI agents accessible across all platforms.

topics.text: Peter previously worked at Blur (makers of Zerro and Blurmy) building AI agents for Web3 actions using natural language prompts.
Slash 2.0 launched a month ago after a complete product rebuild; currently has 60 weekly active users in closed beta before public launch tomorrow.

Slash Pro and Slash Enterprise subscriptions launching tomorrow with a token flywheel mechanism starting with buybacks and burns in phase one, then credit system integration for product payments in future phases.
Grand vision is to make personal AI agents accessible to everyone across all platforms, not confined to a single browser extension or interface.
Agents should focus on performing actions for users rather than just answering questions, aiming to create a Jarvis-like assistant that controls multiple apps across the internet.

l3uDoaza3rs.tldr: Marvin (Hedgemony Fund) is building a Telegram trading bot that executes trades based on news signals, with access initially restricted to token holders with 5 million tokens or more. The most surprising element is his dual flywheel model combining token buyback-and-burn with business revenue buyback, designed to create exponential growth as bot profits fund token purchases.

topics.text: Founder teased a Telegram bot on livestream, received overwhelming demand from users asking how to trade without using the terminal directly.
Bot access restricted to token holders owning 5 million tokens or more, equivalent to 0.5% of total token supply.
Planned buyback and burn mechanism: fees from bot profits will be allocated to buying back and burning the token, with additional unspecified nuances to be announced soon.
Dual flywheel strategy: bot profits generate fees that buy token, creating hype that attracts more users, generating more fees in exponential cycle.
Believe Capital is advising the project and helping plan the flywheel mechanism while founder focuses on building.
Considering staking mechanism that would lower fees for token holders as additional utility beyond buyback and burn.
Founder provided backtesting documents with 70-day timestamps and live platform to prove trades are real, addressing early accusations that the project was fake.

lN7Fi1ZGfQI.tldr: Hedgemony is an AI-powered algorithmic trading bot that scrapes nearly 3,000 news sources to autonomously make long/short trades on crypto markets, claiming 2,000% P&L since launch. Founder Marvin built the system after noticing market correlations with Trump announcements, expanded it globally, and launched on the Believe platform to democratize access to hedge-fund-grade trading signals. The striking claim: the algorithm received news of Iranian missile strikes 2 minutes before Bloomberg Terminal.

topics.text: Founder Marvin's background: switched from pre-med to AI after discovering GPT-3 during a gap year, then spent years building AI and crypto projects before launching Hedgemony.

Initial inspiration came in February after Trump's inauguration, when Marvin noticed Solana price movements correlated with Trump announcements on Truth Social, sparking the idea for a Trump-tracking bot.

The algorithm expanded from Trump to 3,000 news sources globally including Reuters, Bloomberg, and niche sources like Aljazeera Channel 12 in Iran, sometimes capturing news 2 minutes before Bloomberg Terminal.

myzmzDA822A.tldr: Kanye West launched the $YZY token, which crashed immediately after a $415 million 24-hour trading volume, with the host and guests discussing whether markets have matured enough to reject celebrity scam coins like this one and the earlier Trump and Melania tokens.

topics.text: The $YZY token launch was long-anticipated after earlier creator coin waves (Trump, Melania, Libra), but dropped unexpectedly last night.
Kanye's funds from a previous legal case were unfrozen the same day $YZY launched, raising suspicions about the connection and timing.
Token distribution mirrored previous insider scams: 70% to insiders, 10% of liquidity pool, 20% to public, similar to Trump and Libra launches.
A poll showed 80% of traders faded the $YZY trade; most who profited entered in the first two candles when transaction throughput was congested.
A wallet bought at 200 million, secured 1 million profit in 8 minutes, then sent proceeds to a treasury wallet that also received funds from a Libra sniper.

CB14jWy0n3E.tldr: Dan Wee, who works at Meteora on Solana, explains how the launchpad wars began: Meteora's Dynamic Bonding Curve (DBC) technology launched into beta five months ago, enabling any team to quickly spin up a customized launchpad with configurable parameters—and within months, 20+ launchpads built on it, from Pump.fun to Jupiter Studio to Moonshot, each using different curve configurations to differentiate themselves.

topics.text: Dan joined Meteora five months ago when the DBC program went into beta, with zero launchpads using it at the time.
A Dynamic Bonding Curve lets launchpad creators configure curve shape, anti-sniping mechanisms, fees, liquidity depth, and initial vs. graduation market caps—unlike fixed curves like Pump or Raydium.
Meteora grew from zero to 20+ launchpads in five months; currently tracking 200+ Telegram groups of projects wanting to use Meteora's DBC or DMM host.
The three-step process: create a DBC config key specifying curve parameters, launch pools using that key, and provide trading APIs so tokens appear on terminals like Jupe Pro.

dip3t4iHj34.tldr: AD and Joseph discuss SolCypher, a Solana trading bot that evolved from an AI-powered project into a social trading platform with competitive leagues for alpha callers and traders. The founders reveal they've built the product in just six months without external funding, recently pivoted away from AI signals toward human trader verification with a 100% fee-sharing flywheel to token stakers, and hint at major announcements coming in two weeks that could significantly accelerate growth.

topics.text: SolCypher is a trading bot, copy trader, and sniper combining AI with social trading features on Solana.
AD has been programming for 20 years since age 10, in crypto since 2015, and told Joseph about Bitcoin at $1,000; this is their first major Web3 project.
The project pivoted from AI agent signals (35-40% hit rate) to a social trading model based on real alpha callers using SolCypher, noting top 25 callers achieve above 60% success rates.
SolCypher's KO League tracks caller performance with built-in tipping: 25% of trading fees go to the alpha caller who made the first call on a token.
100% of fees after tipping are distributed weekly to CIPHER token stakers; 35% of supply is team-locked, 65% available to community; currently 50% total staked.
Projected daily payouts to stakers would reach approximately $200,000 USD if SolCypher reached Trojan's trading volume levels.
The team is exploring token buyback-and-burn mechanisms tied to specific token communities to incentivize adoption over competing bots.
SolCypher has about 700 users currently; growth was explosive in January-February but has slowed, though daily growth continues and the team is profitable.
Major announcements and new features coming within two weeks, including additional utility and expanded trading league options for different market types.

zqLXbtTcyaQ.tldr: Dan Wee, infrastructure builder at Meteora, discusses how the project's Dynamic Bonding Curve (DBC) technology has enabled the explosion of launchpads on Solana—growing from zero to 30+ in five months. The surprising insight: Meteora doesn't compete with launchpads but empowers them through highly customizable, open-source tools, allowing each to build unique flywheels rather than forcing standardized parameters.

topics.text: Dan joined Meteora five months ago; DBC launched into beta the same week, going from zero launchpad partners to 200+ telegram groups of builders wanting to use the tech.
Dynamic Bonding Curve lets builders customize curve shape, anti-sniping mechanisms, fees, and liquidity depth, unlike fixed-parameter competitors like Pump and Raydium.
Fee scheduler decays taxes over time or slots, with configurable start and end fees; traders can see declining tax on terminals like XM or simulate transactions on Jupe Pro.
Rate limiter uses a tax bracket model: small retail buys get base fees (1%), large sniper buys get incrementally higher fees (up to 4%), depending on reference amount.
Bags, Belief, and Drip Studio use different DBC configurations; Bags built wrapper programs on top to send fees to Twitter accounts and creator pools.
HeavenX built its own in-house AMM to avoid paying Meteora fees but uses standardized 6-second sniper delay, while Meteora offers millisecond-level customization.
Permanently locked liquidity on DBC creates a SOL sink; Trump's pool is permanently locked with no withdrawal mechanism except via massive token sell-off.

iQwYGFnDLyo.tldr: Kled AI, founded by Avi Patel, monetizes streaming data by integrating with Twitch, Kick, and TikTok, allowing creators to upload their streams and earn money; the project just raised at a $40M valuation and hints at upcoming equity financing, with Patel suggesting the token could be tied to company equity through an 'inner capital market' mechanism.

topics.text: Kled integrated with Twitch TV, Kick.com, and TikTok, allowing creators to link accounts and automatically stream data into the Kled marketplace.
Kled built copyright detection software to filter out DMCA-violating content from training data, converting previously unusable streamer data into monetizable datasets.
XQC's 70+ hours per week of streaming over 8 years represents a multi-seven-figure monetizable dataset on Kled, with payment rates expected to exceed $100 for a 3-hour VOD.
Kled Foundation teased an 'equity financing' document on Twitter, hinting at a second funding round after the $40M valuation raise.
Patel stated 'there are mechanisms that can change this' regarding tokenizing equity, and that ICM was meant to align ownership with participation, not just speculation.
A bidding war occurred between two entities for Batch Four data contracts, with the winning bid reaching $150k; Kled plans to create two separate contracts next time to increase batch sizes.
Kled built a marketplace enabling companies like Task Rush to sell specialized labeled data; Task Rush doctors labeling medical data can earn 4x more than generic classification rates.
Kled owns equity stakes in all companies building within its ecosystem, including teams from Google Notebook and Task Rush.
The token is currently valued under $14M despite a $40M valuation for the company and hints of another raise at much higher valuation.

Patel claims streamers could earn $100+ for three-hour uploads, hints at upcoming equity financing at a $40M valuation, and is building a data pipeline ecosystem with companies like Taskrush where specialized labelers can earn premium rates.

topics.text: Kled integrated with Twitch TV, Kick.com, and TikTok so creators can link accounts and automatically stream data into the Kled Marketplace.
Streamers uploading three-hour VODs could earn more than $100, with top streamers potentially in the multisix-figure range from monetizable datasets.
The founder hinted at equity financing in a cryptic tweet from the Kled Foundation account with a blacked-out document, saying 'every major shift starts quietly.'
Kled raised $40 million valuation, with the founder claiming the valuation floor is set by investor expectations for 10x returns, making that the minimum token value.
Maya recently acquired 0.5% equity in Kled and serves as a close adviser to the project.
The founder stated ICM (Interchain Market) mechanisms can align ownership with participation and that equity doesn't need to be tokenized but can be combined with token mechanics.
A bidding war for Batch 4 data reached 150k, with two different entities competing for priority access to fast-sourced training data.
Kled owns stakes in all companies building on its ecosystem, including Taskrush, which labels specialized data with doctors and other professionals earning 4x rates for high-quality datasets.

PhcQTJyWlgs.tldr: Grandmaster is an AI agent launchpad on Solana where users create chess-playing agents by uploading a photo, and the agent's strength is determined by its token's market cap—creating guaranteed price action as agents play games for money. Founder Christian Dittmeier explains how this gamifies token launches by making them feel like creating game characters rather than launching projects, while enabling traders to impact outcomes by buying tokens to boost their agent's ELO rating.

topics.text: Grandmaster gamifies market caps by tying AI agents that play chess to token trading, creating guaranteed price action instead of static launchpad tokens.
Chess has 600 million players globally, with chess.com having over 100 million paid subscribers and major creators drawing millions of views, making it an ideal game for the platform.
ELO rating ranges from 200 to 3,000 on chess.com, with amateur players between 1,000-2,000 and titled players above 2,000; expected win probability is calculated based on ELO difference.
Christian and co-founders previously built Evaluate for NBA Top Shot NFTs (raised $6 million), pivoted to NFT swapping, and won an Alliance hackathon in February for Grandmaster.
When launching an agent, creators receive 0.5% of trading fees plus all game winnings, while other traders can speculate on tokens like any memecoin.
An agent's market cap directly determines its ELO strength move-by-move; buyers can increase market cap during games to make their agent play stronger and impact outcomes.
The platform has 200 agents with 150k in volume after one week, and the model could generate $1.4 million in guaranteed weekly volume at 2,000 agents.
Future plans include referral incentive systems, charts, token graduation to Raydium or Meteora at certain market caps, and expansion to other games like poker.
Human vs. agent play is being considered but poses cheating risks; Christian is exploring options like paying to play one move or rolling moves without disadvantaging genuine users.
Grandmaster destigmatizes token launching by framing agents as game characters rather than projects, attracting users from NBA Top Shot and making the first crypto platform experience for many.

c8_sczVlVro.tldr: Vibhu, product marketing lead at Solana Foundation, discusses Internet Capital Markets (ICM) and how platforms like Believe are democratizing access to private company investments through tokenization. He argues that for ICM to scale from current $130M to billions in capital, tokens must be tied to equity with legal protections and corporate accountability—not just speculative trading vehicles—and warns that without real value guarantees, 95% of current token promises will likely be broken.

topics.text: Ash Boden at Solana Foundation coined the term 'Internet Capital Markets' in November to describe how anyone with an internet connection can participate in capital markets that were previously US-centric and inaccessible to most people and companies globally.

Drip was the top crypto collectibles platform where creators minted 300 million collectibles on-chain and earned approximately $15 million total before being sold to Jupiter, which now owns and operates it.

Believe works as a fair-launch platform using bonding curves starting at 5k market cap, with all capital from purchases becoming liquidity in underlying AMMs rather than the traditional ICO model where companies raise and spend capital directly.
Soju proposed token holders could receive equity stakes (20% in his example) through a foundation structure and elect board members, creating alignment between token holders and company governance.

Vibhu estimates 95% of token promises companies make—like concert tickets, merchandise, and platform benefits—will be broken because they lack legal enforcement mechanisms and corporate accountability structures.

Solana Foundation has successfully brought 80 Real World Assets (RWAs) on-chain from major financial institutions, representing tokenization of stocks, bonds, money markets, and other financial products worth tens of trillions in potential volume.

SHaUpI7qAUE.tldr: RatSpeak is an offline-capable, encrypted mesh network protocol built on top of Reticulum that supports multiple transport layers (LoRa, Bluetooth, TCP) for peer-to-peer communication without relying on traditional internet infrastructure. Founder dude has spent nearly 10 years in crypto and was inspired by Meshtastic to build something more complete; the project launched a token in May that has recently seen significant growth, with the founder holding about 5% of supply and exploring tokenomics around incentivizing network nodes and enabling offline AI agent communication.

topics.text: Founder dude has spent 10 years in crypto, starting with Bitcoin in high school and working at Kyber Network during the ICO era, then at Aave during their lend-to-aave token swap.
RatSpeak is built on Reticulum protocol and supports multiple transport layers including LoRa, Bluetooth, TCP, and Wi-Fi, unlike Meshtastic which only supports LoRa.
RatSpeak enables end-to-end encrypted mesh networking where an offline Android phone with Bluetooth can gain internet access through an iPhone also on the mesh that has internet connectivity.
Practical use cases include two canoes in Boundary Waters with no cell service communicating via $5 radio devices, and Bluetooth mesh at events like Burning Man or underground raves.
LoRa has line-of-sight requirements and ranges of tens of kilometers, while Bluetooth low energy reaches about 30 meters with faster data transfer.
The token was launched a few months back without the founder's knowledge by community members, which frustrated him initially, but the fees generated have helped fund infrastructure and development.

Founder owns approximately 5% of the total token supply and is exploring ways to bring tokens back into the network through incentivizing propagation nodes, transport nodes, and potentially AI agent micropayments.
Fee revenues are being used for infrastructure costs, 3D-printed node giveaways at hackathons, and plans to install a LoRa node on Lookout Mountain or in Golden, Colorado to oversee Denver coverage.
RatSpeak is already shipping on every operating system including iOS via test flight, with hundreds to perhaps a thousand active participants currently on the network.
Future vision includes FCC licensing for official hardware devices, baking token incentives into the network, and encouraging more developers to build on the RatSpeak protocol.
